definition_zh: 翅膀；机翼；（建筑的）侧翼；派别；（剧场）侧幕
definition_en: the limb a bird or insect uses to fly, and similar flat parts: an aircraft wing, a side of a building or a group inside a party
core_image: 一只鸟在起飞前一瞬把双翅完全张开，风从羽尖下面钻过去
scene: 堤岸上，那只白鸟把双翅完全张开，只一振就离开了栏杆。 The bird spread its wings and rose over the river without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 wing 是「翅膀」（第 1 个义项：鸟或昆虫用来飞的肢体）；句意为那只鸟张开双翅，无声地升到河面上。起飞前双翅完全张开的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 飞；给…装翅膀；（口语）即兴说

senses.title: The limb that lifts a bird
senses.definition: the feathered limb of a bird or the thin flying part of an insect
senses.definitionCN: 鸟的覆羽肢体，或昆虫薄薄的飞行器官
senses.example: The bird spread its wings and rose over the river without a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟张开双翅，无声地升到河面上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the body part, named from the flapping side pieces that a bird carries.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是身体部位，得名于鸟身上那两片扑动的侧片。

senses.title: The lifting surface of a plane
senses.definition: the long flat part sticking out on each side of an aircraft that holds it up in the air
senses.definitionCN: 飞机两侧伸出的长而平的部件，使飞机升空
senses.example: Ice on the wings delayed the flight for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 机翼结冰让航班延误了一个小时。
senses.why: When people built flying machines they took the shape of the bird, and the name came with the shape.
senses.whyCN: 人们造飞行器时借用了鸟的形状，名字也跟着形状一起搬了过来。

senses.title: A side part of a building
senses.definition: a part of a large building that sticks out from the main block
senses.definitionCN: 大型建筑从主体伸出的那部分
senses.example: The library occupies the east wing of the old palace.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆占了旧宫殿的东侧翼。
senses.why: A side piece spreading out from a body looks like a wing on a bird, so architecture borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 从主体伸出去的侧片很像鸟翼，于是建筑也借用了这个词。

senses.title: A group inside a party
senses.definition: one of the groups inside a political party or a movement, holding a distinct view
senses.definitionCN: 政党或运动内部持有不同主张的一组人
senses.example: The moderate wing of the party opposed the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 党内的温和派反对这项新税。
senses.why: A party spreads out on both sides like a pair of wings, and each side got a name of its own.
senses.whyCN: 党派像一对翅膀分向两侧展开，每一侧都得到了自己的名字。

intro.en: Wing is an old Germanic word for the flying limb, related to the verb that meant to flutter; the Norse form had a soft g that eventually fell silent.
intro.cn: wing 是日耳曼语中表示飞行肢体的老词，与意为「扑翅」的动词同源；诺斯语形式的软 g 后来不发音了。

items.en: A common Germanic root named the wing and the act of flapping it.
items.cn: 一个共同的日耳曼词根既指翅膀，也指扑动它的动作。

items.en: The Norse vængr carried a soft g, and this form entered English lands in the north.
items.cn: 诺斯语 vængr 带有软 g，这一形式进入了北方的英格兰地区。

items.en: The native word for wing was feþera, feather, which survived only in the sense of plumage.
items.cn: 古英语本土表示翅膀的词是 feþera（羽毛），只在羽饰义上存活下来。

items.en: The Norse word became the standard wing, and buildings took it for their side parts.
items.cn: 诺斯语词成为标准的 wing，建筑也借它表示侧部。

items.en: Aviation made wing mean the lifting surface, and politics gave each faction a wing of its own.
items.cn: 航空时代让 wing 指升力面，政治又让每个派别各自拥有一翼。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike short words, the second body parts and surfaces with a similar job.
note.cn: 第一组收形近短词，第二组收职司相似的部位与面。

entries.definition: To come out first in a contest.
To complain in a tiresome way.
To move back and forth from a fixed point.
A male ruler of a country.
One of the light plates covering a bird.
A thin limb a fish uses to steer.
The side of an animal or an army.

normalIntro.en: Wing is short and ends in a soft -ng, the sound of something spreading out.
normalIntro.cn: wing 很短，收在软的 -ng 上，像东西展开时的声音。

normal.en: The -ng ending hums, like air under a lifted feather.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ng 嗡嗡地响，像羽毛下钻过的空气。

normal.en: Win plus g: you win with a pair of wings, not a single one.
normal.cn: win 加一个 g：靠一对翅膀才赢，单只不够。

normal.en: Swing contains wing, and a wing swings the air.
normal.cn: swing 里含着 wing，翅膀正是把空气拨开的那个东西。

normal.en: A plane wing and a palace wing share the same simple picture: a part sticking out sideways.
normal.cn: 机翼与宫殿侧翼共享同一个简单形象：向侧面伸出去的一块。

normal.en: Under someone's wing is to be sheltered, as chicks under a folded one.
normal.cn: be under someone's wing 是被庇护，就像雏鸟躲在收拢的翼下。

abstract.en: Two shapes unfolding to the full width at once.
abstract.cn: 两个形状在同一瞬间展开到最宽。

abstract.en: The moment after leaving a railing, when no ground is touched.
abstract.cn: 离开栏杆之后、还没碰上任何地面的那一刻。

abstract.en: A shadow passing over a path with no sound attached.
abstract.cn: 一道影子从小径上掠过，却没有附带任何声音。

examples.en: A moth with pale wings knocked against the lamp.
examples.cn: 一只浅色翅膀的蛾子撞在灯上。

examples.en: She was taken under the wing of an older musician.
examples.cn: 她被一位年长的音乐家收在门下。

examples.en: The hospital added a new wing last year.
examples.cn: 医院去年加建了一座侧楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: wing 结尾的 -ng 像翅膀震动时的嗡声。

root: 日耳曼语词根（翼、扑翅）→ 古诺斯语 vængr → 中古英语 winge → wing；同族有 winged、wingless。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a bird's limb, extends to machines of flight, to the sides of buildings, then to the sides of a party.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从鸟的肢体开始，扩展到飞行机械，再到建筑的侧部，最后到党派的阵营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two feathered shapes unfolded at the moment of take-off.
core.cn: 核心意象：起飞一瞬完全展开的两片羽翼。

branches.en: The bird branch: a white bird rising over the river.
branches.cn: 鸟类分支：白鸟从河面升起。

branches.en: The flying machine branch: ice on the wings of an aircraft.
branches.cn: 飞行器分支：机翼上的冰。

branches.en: The building branch: the east wing of a palace.
branches.cn: 建筑分支：宫殿的东侧翼。

branches.en: The political branch: the moderate wing of a party.
branches.cn: 政治分支：党内的温和派。

branches.en: The shape branch: everything is a part that spreads sideways.
branches.cn: 形状分支：一切都成了向侧面铺开的部分。

intro.en: Wing is a bare Germanic noun that takes common endings and makes compounds such as wingless and wingman.
intro.cn: wing 是光秃的日耳曼名词，能接常见词尾，也能构成 wingless、wingman 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The stem has no Latin source; ala, the Latin word for wing, appears only in scientific and borrowed shapes.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语的 ala（翼）只出现在科学与借入的形式里。

items.example: It is the plain noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它既是朴素的动词也是名词。

items.example: The side sense moved into politics.
The picture of chicks under feathers.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟躲在羽毛下的画面。

definition_zh: 第九；九分之一
definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighth; one of nine equal parts
core_image: 九级台阶的最上面放着一块小小的铜牌，牌上刻着一条横线
scene: 楼道里的九级台阶被擦得很亮，最上面一级放着一块小小的铜牌。 He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
sceneCN: 这里是「第九层」（第 1 个义项：序数第九）；句意是他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。图中可辨识物件：九级台阶、铜牌、楼道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 ninth 加 -ly 构成，义为「第九（用于列举）」
ninth 的基数形式，古英语 nigon 一路传下来，义为「九」

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第八之后的数
senses.example: He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。
senses.why: Ninth is nine plus the old ordinal ending -th, the same ending that makes fourth from four; the ending marks a place in a line, not a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninth 是 nine 加古老的序数词尾 -th，和 four 变 fourth 用的是同一个词尾；这个词尾标出的是一列中的位置，而不是一个新数量。

senses.title: One of nine equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nine equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A ninth of the students chose the longer course.
senses.exampleCN: 九分之一的学生选了那门较长的课程。
senses.why: The ordinal ending also cuts: a ninth is what one gets when a whole is split nine ways, which is why the rank word and the fraction word look identical.
senses.whyCN: 这个序数词尾同时也起切割作用：把整体分成九份，得到的就是 a ninth，所以表示名次的词和表示分数的词长得一模一样。

intro.en: Ninth is the ordinal of nine, formed in Old English by a unit numeral plus the ending that marks rank, then trimmed into its modern spelling.
intro.cn: ninth 是九的序数词，在古英语里由个位数词加表名次的词尾构成，后来缩减成今天的拼写。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的；确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的形式。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of the whole ordinal family.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是整个序数词族的底座。

items.en: The ordinal added the -þa ending used for ranking, giving the ancestor of ninth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -þa，形成 ninth 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English shortened and respelled the word as ninthe, and the modern consonant pattern was already visible.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短并改写为 ninthe，现代的辅音格局那时已经看得出来。

items.en: Modern English fixes the spelling ninth and uses it both for rank and for the fraction one of nine equal parts.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 ninth，并用它同时表示名次与九等份中的一份。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its teen, tens, ordinal and adverb forms; the near-meaning group places ninth between its neighbours and next to the idea of a fraction.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个「九」的底座，收十几、十位、序数与副词形式；近义组把 ninth 放到相邻序数之间，并与分数的概念放在一起。

entries.definition: The teen form of nine, built with -teen instead of the ordinal ending.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十几形式，用 -teen 而不是序数词尾构成。

entries.definition: The tens form of nine, built with -ty.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on ninth with -ly, used in lists.
entries.definitionCN: ninth 加 -ly 构成的副词，用于列举。

entries.definition: The ordinal for ninety, part of the same -th family.
entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，属同一 -th 词族。

entries.definition: The ordinal just before ninth in the same line.
entries.definitionCN: 同一序列中紧挨在第九之前的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal just after ninth, closing the single digits.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第九之后的序数词，为个位数的结尾。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position, the class of ninth.
entries.definitionCN: 标出位置的数词，ninth 所属的类别。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, the kind of quantity one ninth expresses.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一份，正是九分之一所表达的量。

normalIntro.en: The word is nine wearing the ordinary English rank ending, and the same form serves as a rank and as a share because the ending does both jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」披上寻常的英语名次词尾；同一个形式既是名次也是一份，因为这个词尾兼做两件事。

normal.en: Nine plus -th is the same pattern as four plus -th; ninth is the ninth place, not a new quantity.
normal.cn: 九加 -th 和四加 -th 是同一个模式；ninth 是第九个位置，不是一个新数量。

normal.en: The old ordinal ending survives in modern English even though the Old English spelling has been trimmed away.
normal.cn: 古老的序数词尾在现代英语里仍然活着，尽管古英语的拼写已经被削掉。

normal.en: Ninth also divides: cut a whole into nine equal pieces and each piece is a ninth.
normal.cn: ninth 也用来分：把整体切成九个等份，每一份就是一个 ninth。

normal.en: Ninthly is built on ninth with -ly, the way English turns an ordinal into a list marker.
normal.cn: ninthly 是在 ninth 后加 -ly 造出来的，英语就这样把序数变成列举时的标记。

normal.en: Dates and floors use the bare ordinal, so on the ninth or the ninth floor needs no extra noun.
normal.cn: 日期和楼层都用光秃秃的序数词，所以 on the ninth 或 the ninth floor 不用再加名词。

abstract.en: One short ending does two jobs at once, ranking a floor and cutting a cake, which is why the same word can point in two directions.
abstract.cn: 一个短词尾同时干两件事：给楼层排名，把蛋糕切开，所以同一个词能指向两个方向。

abstract.en: Ninth is the last single-digit ordinal, so it sounds like the end of the simplest counting line.
abstract.cn: ninth 是个位数里的最后一个序数词，听起来像最简单那条计数线的收尾。

abstract.en: The word barely changed shape across a thousand years, which makes it a small fossil of how English counts.
abstract.cn: 这个词一千年里形状几乎没变，因此它是英语如何计数的一小块化石。

examples.en: He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
examples.cn: 他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。

examples.en: A ninth of the students chose the longer course.
examples.cn: 九分之一的学生选了那门较长的课程。

examples.en: The new lease begins on the ninth of May.
examples.cn: 新租约从五月九日开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈恩丝」——九级台阶爬到顶，铜牌上刻着第九；ninth 就是第九、九分之一。

root: 古英语 nigon（九）加序数词尾 -þa 构成 nigoþa，中古英语作 ninthe，现代英语定为 ninth；与拉丁语 novem 同出原始印欧语数词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ninth place in a line; the same form then names one of nine equal parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一列中的第九位；同一个形式再指九等份里的一份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brass plate lying on the top of nine polished steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：九级擦亮的台阶顶上放着一块小铜牌。

branches.en: a brass plate on the top of nine steps
a lift stopping at the ninth floor
a cake cut into nine equal slices
the same short word ranking a place and naming a share
branches.cn: 同一个短词既给位置排名，也命名一份

branches.en: a date circled on the ninth of the month
branches.cn: 日历上被圈出的那个月的第九天

intro.en: The word is the Old English nine plus an ordinal ending, and the modern form still carries the endings that make its adverb and plural.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语的「九」加一个序数词尾，现代形式还带着构成副词与复数的词尾。

latinIntro.en: English nine and Latin novem descend from the same ancient Indo-European numeral, so the Latin forms are cognates for comparison, not the source of ninth.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 同出古老的原始印欧语数词，因此下列拉丁形式只是同源对照，不是 ninth 的来源。

definition_zh: 最后的；最终的；决定性的；决赛
definition_en: coming at the end, not to be changed, or the last game of a contest
core_image: 画上句号的那一笔：前面再长，都归结到终点
scene: 比分牌上两支队伍追平，只剩最后一投。 The final shot decided the whole match.
sceneCN: 这里 final 是「决定性的、最后的」（第 1 个义项：在最后且不可更改）；句意为最后一投决定了整场比赛。

pos.zh: 形容词：最后的；最终的；决定性的
名词：决赛；期末考试（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀，义为「最后；终于」
加动词后缀，义为「把……最后定下来」
同根借自意大利语，指乐章或演出的终场
加施动者后缀，指进入决赛的选手

senses.title: Coming at the end
senses.definition: happening or coming at the end of a series or process
senses.definitionCN: 出现在一系列事物的末尾
senses.example: The final bus leaves at eleven.
senses.exampleCN: 末班车十一点发车。
senses.why: The core image is the closing stroke of a series, so the first sense marks the end slot.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一连串事物的收尾一笔，第一个义项标记终点位置。

senses.title: Decided and not to be changed
senses.definition: fixed and impossible to change after discussion
senses.definitionCN: 一经作出便不可再改
senses.example: The judge's word was final.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的话是最终裁定。
senses.why: What ends the process also closes the argument.
senses.whyCN: 结束流程的东西也终结了争论，于是有定论义。

senses.title: The last game of a competition
senses.definition: the last and deciding game or round of a contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中最后一场、定胜负的一轮
senses.example: Our team reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队打进了决赛。
senses.why: The end slot of the contest gets its own name.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的终点位置单独得名，成了名词决赛。

senses.title: End-of-term examinations
senses.definition: the important examinations at the end of a school term or course
senses.definitionCN: 学期或课程末尾的重要考试
senses.example: Finals week is the quietest week on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 考试周是校园里最安静的一周。
senses.why: Another end point of school life takes the same closing word.
senses.whyCN: 校园生活的另一个终点套用了同一个收尾词。

intro.en: Final traces back to Latin finis, the word for an end or boundary.
intro.cn: final 溯源到拉丁语 finis，表示终点、边界。

items.en: Latin finis meant an end or limit, and finalis meant relating to the end.
items.cn: 拉丁语 finis 指终点或界限，finalis 表示与终点相关。

items.en: Finalis stayed in learned use for anything at the end.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 finalis 在书面语中指处于末尾之物。

items.en: Old French final carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 古法语 final 把这个词带向英语。

items.en: Middle English final meant last in order or time.
items.cn: 中古英语 final 表示顺序或时间上的最后。

items.en: The contest and exam senses developed in the modern period.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出决赛与期末考试义。

note.en: Final, last and ultimate sit in the same corner of meaning.
note.cn: final、last、ultimate 挤在同一个意义角落。

entries.definition: adverb meaning at last
the closing part of a performance
the ornament on top of a spire; only one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 尖顶饰；与 final 仅差一字母，词义无关

entries.definition: the everyday word for coming after all others
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词：排在所有其他之后的

entries.definition: formal word for the greatest or final degree
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语：终极的、最后的

entries.definition: at the very end, often of a route or disease
entries.definitionCN: 极终的；常指线路或病程的末端

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to finish off final.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子给 final 收尾。

normal.en: Final shares its root with finish and fine: an end line.
normal.cn: final 与 finish、fine 同根：一条终点线。

normal.en: The final whistle ends the football match.
normal.cn: 终场哨声结束足球赛。

normal.en: When a decision is final, the door is shut.
normal.cn: 决定一旦 final，门就关上了。

normal.en: Reaching the final means you survived every earlier round.
normal.cn: 打进决赛意味着你赢下了之前每一轮。

normal.en: Finals week fills the library with tired students.
normal.cn: 期末考试周把图书馆塞满疲惫的学生。

abstract.en: Final is the full stop at the end of a long sentence.
abstract.cn: final 是长句末尾的句号。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line tape stretched across the road.
abstract.cn: 想象横在路面上的终点线带。

abstract.en: Everything before it exists so that the final can arrive.
abstract.cn: 之前的一切都是为了迎接 final 的到来。

definition_zh: 正确的；改正；纠正
definition_en: right and without mistakes; to make something right
core_image: 老师用红笔把错字圈出来，写上正确答案
scene: 发数学卷子时，同桌发现自己把小数点点错了位置。 The teacher corrected the mistake with her red pen.
sceneCN: 这里 correct 是动词「改正」（第 4 个义项：使变得正确）；句意是老师用红笔改正了错误。

derivatives.zh: 由 correct 加 -ion 构成，义为「改正；批改」
由 correct 加 -ly 构成，义为「正确地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不正确的」

senses.title: Right; without mistakes
senses.definition: right according to facts or rules
senses.definitionCN: 符合事实或规则
senses.example: Your spelling is all correct this time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次你的拼写全对。
senses.why: The root means made straight, and straight work has no bends or errors.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「扶正」，笔直的答卷没有弯折和错误。

senses.title: Proper; socially suitable
senses.definition: suitable for a situation or polite behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 适合场合或礼貌的行为
senses.example: Wearing a tie is correct for the speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲比赛打领带是得体的。
senses.why: A straight, upright posture is also what society calls proper.
senses.whyCN: 端正的姿态也是社会认可的得体。

senses.title: To point out and fix mistakes
senses.definition: to show someone their mistakes and make them right
senses.definitionCN: 指出错误并使之正确
senses.example: Our teacher corrects our essays every week.
senses.exampleCN: 老师每周批改我们的作文。
senses.why: Correcting straightens the crooked part of an answer.
senses.whyCN: 纠正是把答案中歪斜的部分扶直。

senses.title: To make something right
senses.definition: to change something so that it becomes right
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变使某事变得正确
senses.example: Please correct the wrong numbers in this report.
senses.exampleCN: 请改正报告里的错误数字。
senses.why: The verb keeps its Latin force: to set straight what bent.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留拉丁语的力度：把弯的东西扳直。

intro.en: Correct literally means made straight again.
intro.cn: correct 的字面意思是「重新扶正」。

items.en: The Latin verb corrigere meant to make straight, from com- (intensive) + regere (to make straight, rule).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 corrigere 意为扶正，由 com-（加强）+ regere（使直、统治）构成。

items.en: The past participle correctus described what had been set straight.
items.cn: 过去分词 correctus 描述已被扶正之物。

items.en: French carried correger and related forms into scholarship.
items.cn: 法语把 correger 等形式带入学术语。

items.en: English adopted correct in the fourteenth century for fixing texts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 correct，用于校订文本。

items.en: Today it covers school marks, manners and even politics.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖分数、礼仪乃至政治语境。

note.en: These words share the reg root of ruling straight, or mark rightness.
note.cn: 这些词共享 reg（使直、统治）词根，或表示正确。

wrong; the in- flips the meaning
straight, without turning

correct; true

normalIntro.cn: correct 就是「被扶正」的词。

normal.en: correct = com- (fully) + regere (make straight).
normal.cn: correct 由 com-（完全）+ regere（使直）构成。

normal.en: direct and erect share the reg root.
normal.cn: direct 和 erect 同享 reg 词根。

normal.en: in- makes incorrect, the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 in- 构成 incorrect，反义词。

normal.en: correct mistakes means fix them.
normal.cn: correct mistakes 指改正错误。

normal.en: correct sounds like kerect; an erect posture helps correct answers.
normal.cn: correct 音近「可睿克特」，睿智作答全对。

abstract.en: Picture a red tick beside every right answer.
abstract.cn: 想象每个正确答案旁的红勾。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked fence straightened post by post.
abstract.cn: 想象歪斜的篱笆被一根根扶正。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing a perfectly straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子画出笔直的线。

examples.en: Choose the correct word for each blank in the exercise.
examples.cn: 在练习中为每个空选出正确的单词。

examples.en: The teacher corrected my pronunciation of Thursday.
examples.cn: 老师纠正了我 Thursday 的发音。

examples.en: Reading the question twice helps you give correct answers.
examples.cn: 把题目读两遍有助于给出正确答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可瑞克」——可瑞克同学答题又快又对，全卷 correct。

root: 拉丁语 corrigere（扶正），由 com-（加强）+ regere（使直；统治）构成。reg 词根同族词有 direct（直接的）、erect（直立的）、regulate（管理）。

sensesIntro.en: From made-straight to right, proper and fixing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「扶正」引申为正确、得体与纠正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: setting crooked things straight
core.cn: 核心意象：把歪的东西扳直

branches.en: Free of mistakes.
Suitable for the occasion.
Pointing out others' errors.
Changing things to be right.
Straightening ends in rightness.

intro.en: The reg root of ruling straight governs a large family.
intro.cn: reg（使直、统治）词根管辖一个大家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere means to make straight or rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere 意为使直、统治。

definition_zh: 印刷；印出；打印；打印件；版画；印记；出版；刊登
definition_en: to put words or pictures onto paper with ink and a press; to make a paper copy from a computer; a mark left by pressure; a picture taken from a prepared plate
core_image: 油墨压上纸面，字从凸起的铅字里翻出来
scene: 窗外雨声不停，车间里的机器一下一下压着纸，油墨味顺着门缝散出去。 Every morning the shop would print the day's notices for the whole town.
sceneCN: 这里 print 是「印刷、印出」（第 1 个义项：把油墨压到纸上）；句意为这家店每天早上为全镇印当天的通告。图中可辨识物件：压纸的机器、油墨、门缝。

pos.zh: 印刷；印出；打印；出版；刊登
印刷；印出的字；打印件；版画；印记；指纹

derivatives.zh: 由 print 加 -er 构成，义为「印刷工；打印机」
由 print 加 -ing 构成，义为「印刷；印刷术」
由 print 加 -able 构成，义为「可印刷的；适合刊登的」
由前缀 im-（进入）加 print 构成，义为「压印；留下印记」

senses.title: To press ink onto paper
senses.definition: to produce words or pictures on paper by pressing an inked surface against it
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸了油墨的印版压向纸面，从而产生文字或图像
senses.example: The old press can print a thousand sheets in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老印刷机一小时能印一千张。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to press, so the action begins as pressure on an inked surface rather than as writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个动作的起点是把蘸墨的表面压下去，而不是拿笔去写。

senses.title: To make a copy from a computer
senses.definition: to send a document from a computer to a machine that puts it on paper; also the paper copy so produced
senses.definitionCN: 把电脑里的文件送到机器上输出到纸上；也指这样得到的纸质件
senses.example: Could you print two copies of the report for the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 你能把报告打印两份带到会上吗？
senses.why: When computers entered the office, the same pressing action was handed to a printer, so the old verb was reused for the new machine.
senses.whyCN: 电脑进入办公室之后，同样的「压」交给打印机去完成，于是旧动词被直接借来指这台新机器干的事。

senses.title: A picture made from a plate
senses.definition: a picture produced by pressing an inked block, plate or screen onto paper, usually as one of a set
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸墨的木板、金属版或丝网压在纸上得到的图画，通常成套制作
senses.example: She hung a woodcut print above the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书桌上方挂了一幅木刻版画。
senses.why: Because the method repeats an image from a prepared surface, the noun names the picture that comes off the plate rather than the plate itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种方法是用准备好的版面反复复制图像，名词指的是从版上揭下来的那张画，而不是版本身。

senses.title: A mark left by pressure
senses.definition: a mark pressed into a surface by something touching it, such as a fingerprint or a footprint
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触表面时压出的痕迹，如指纹或脚印
senses.example: The police found a clear print on the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在玻璃上找到一枚清晰的指纹。
senses.why: Long before paper printing, the word meant the impression left by a stamp, and that older sense survives in fingerprints and footprints.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张印刷出现之前很久，这个词就指图章压出的痕迹，这个更早的意思活到了指纹、脚印这类说法里。

senses.title: To publish or carry in a paper
senses.definition: to include a piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or book so that the public can read it
senses.definitionCN: 把一篇文字收进报纸、杂志或书里，让公众读到
senses.example: The paper decided to print her letter on the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报社决定把她的来信登在头版。
senses.why: Publishing in the age of the press meant physically printing the text, so the machine's action became the word for making writing public.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷时代，发表文字就等于把文字真正印出来，于是机器的动作变成了「让文字公开」的说法。

intro.en: Print came into English as a noun for a pressed mark, from a French word for pressing, and only later grew the senses of printing text and pictures.
intro.cn: print 最初以名词身份进入英语，指压出来的痕迹，来自法语中表示「压」的词，后来才长出印文字、印图画的义项。

items.en: Premere meant to press or squeeze, and its participle pressus left marks on several European words.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」，它的分词 pressus 在多种欧洲语言里留下了痕迹。

items.en: Old French preindre, to press, formed the feminine past participle preinte, a thing pressed or stamped.
items.cn: 古法语动词 preindre 意为「压」，其阴性过去分词 preinte 指被压出、被盖上印记的东西。

items.en: The noun preinte named the impression itself, the mark that a seal or a block leaves behind.
items.cn: 名词 preinte 指印记本身，即印章或印版留下的那道痕迹。

items.en: Middle English took the word as print or prent, meaning a mark or stamp, and by the fifteenth century also a printed book.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 print 或 prent，指印记或图章，到十五世纪也指印出来的书。

items.en: With the printing press the verb spread to text and pictures, and in the computer age it was extended to paper output from a screen.
items.cn: 随着印刷机的普及，动词用法扩展到文字与图画；到了电脑时代，又扩展到屏幕上输出到纸面的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on print and its verb stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for making text or images public.
note.cn: 形近组收由 print 及其动词词干构成的词；近义组收表示让文字或图像公之于众的动词。

entries.definition: A person whose trade is printing, or a machine that prints.
entries.definitionCN: 以印刷为业的人，或能打印的机器。

entries.definition: The act or trade of producing text and pictures with a press.
entries.definitionCN: 用印版制作文字与图画的行为或行业；印刷术。

entries.definition: Suitable or safe to be printed and shown to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 适合印出公开的；可以刊印的。

entries.definition: To press a mark into a surface, or the mark so made.
entries.definitionCN: 把痕迹压进表面，或这样留下的痕迹。

entries.definition: To make a piece of writing available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 让一篇文字面向公众发行。

entries.definition: To make a version of something that matches the original.
entries.definitionCN: 做出与原物一致的复制品。

entries.definition: To press a design onto a surface with a tool.
entries.definitionCN: 用工具把图案压到表面上。

entries.definition: To make a copy of an image or text.

normalIntro.en: The word began as the mark left by pressure and then moved to the machine that presses ink onto paper, so every sense is about transfer.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初指压力留下的痕迹，后来转指把油墨压到纸上的机器，所以每个义项讲的都是「转移」。

normal.en: Print comes from a verb for pressing, so the word still remembers the weight of a plate on paper.
normal.cn: print 出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个词至今记得印版压在纸上的分量。

normal.en: A printer is the thing that presses, and also the person whose trade was pressing.
normal.cn: printer 既是压印的机器，也是以压印为业的人。

normal.en: In print means the text has been pressed and is now public; out of print means the plates are no longer run.
normal.cn: in print 指文字已经印出、公开流传；out of print 指版子不再开印。

normal.en: Fine print is the small type at the bottom of a page, the part most people skip.
normal.cn: fine print 是页面底部的小字，多数人会跳过去不读。

normal.en: A fingerprint is literally a print made by a finger, the oldest sense still in daily use.
normal.cn: fingerprint 字面就是手指压出的印子，这是至今仍在日常使用的最古老义项。

abstract.en: Every sense of print is a transfer: ink to paper, screen to page, finger to glass.
abstract.cn: print 的每个义项都是一次转移：油墨到纸上，屏幕到纸面，手指到玻璃。

abstract.en: The word treats an image and a text alike, because both are pressed from one surface onto another.
abstract.cn: 这个词把图像和文字一视同仁，因为两者都是从一面压到另一面。

abstract.en: When a newspaper prints a letter, the physical act and the public act share one verb.
abstract.cn: 当报社 print 一封来信时，物理动作与公开行为共用一个动词。

examples.en: They print the school newspaper every Friday.
examples.cn: 他们每周五印校报。

examples.en: He printed the tickets and put them in an envelope.
examples.cn: 他把票打印出来放进信封。

examples.en: Her first novel is still in print after thirty years.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说三十年后仍在印行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普林特」——谐音像「铺林纸」，把纸一张张贴着铺开，一排排字就被压了上去。

root: 拉丁语 premere（压）→ 古法语 preindre / 名词 preinte（压出的痕迹）→ 中古英语 print；核心始终是「压出来的痕与字」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a mark made by pressure; from that the senses run to ink on paper, computer output, pictures from a plate, fingerprints and published text.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是压力留下的痕迹；义项由此通向纸上的油墨、电脑输出、版上揭下的画、指纹，以及公开的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ink pressed onto paper, letters lifting off raised type.
core.cn: 核心意象：油墨压上纸面，字从凸起的铅字里翻出来。

a letter carried to the front page
a printer spitting out two copies

a thumb mark left on glass

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb premere, to press, has the participle pressus, which also lies behind the English word press.

definition_zh: 关系；关联；恋爱关系
definition_en: the way two people or groups deal with each other over time; a connection between two things; a romantic partnership
core_image: 两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮
scene: 靠窗摆着两把旧椅子，中间那块地板被来回走动磨得发亮。 They built a working relationship over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 relationship 是「关系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间长期相处的方式）；句意为他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。画面里可留意：靠得很近的两把椅子、磨亮的地板。

senses.title: A connection between people
senses.definition: the way two people or groups behave toward each other over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或群体在一段时间里彼此相处的方式
senses.example: They built a working relationship over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns a relation into a continuing state, so the word names something kept up over time rather than a single link.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把 relation 变成一种持续的状态，因此这个词指的是长期维持的东西，而不是一次性的连接。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two facts, amounts, or ideas are connected
senses.definitionCN: 两个事实、数量或观念相互联系的方式
senses.example: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。
senses.why: Things, like people, can be set beside each other, and the line between them is also called a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 事物和人一样可以被并置，而它们之间的那条线也叫 relationship。

senses.title: A romantic partnership
senses.definition: a close personal connection in which two people love each other
senses.definitionCN: 两人彼此相爱的一种亲密关系
senses.example: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
senses.exampleCN: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。
senses.why: When the personal connection is the closest kind, the general word is used without any further qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 当这种私人联系是最亲密的一种时，这个泛称就不再加任何限定词。

intro.en: Relationship is relation plus the old English suffix of state: a link that is kept going, not a link merely drawn.
intro.cn: relationship 是 relation 加上古英语表状态的后缀：一条被持续维持的线，而不是仅仅画出的线。

items.en: Relatio meant a bringing back and a connection between things.
items.cn: relatio 意为带回，以及事物之间的关联。

items.en: English relation named a connection, a report, and a kinsman.
items.cn: 英语 relation 指关联、报告与亲属。

items.en: The Old English suffix -ship means a state or a condition, as in friendship and hardship.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -ship 意为状态或境况，如 friendship 与 hardship。

items.en: Putting -ship on relation produced a word for a connection that lasts and is maintained.
items.cn: 把 -ship 加在 relation 上，造出了表示持久且被维系的关系的词。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the ordinary term for a couple's partnership.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为指伴侣关系的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same connection family; the near-meaning group gathers words for ties and partnerships.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「联系」词族的词；近义组收表示纽带与伴侣关系的词。

entries.definition: A connection or a relative.
A member of one's family.
Compared with something else.
A link between things or people.
A strong feeling that ties people.
A relationship of working together.
A romantic relationship, often secret.

normalIntro.en: The word is a relation with a duration: something two sides keep up, day after day.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是有时间长度的 relation：双方一天天维持下去的东西。

normal.en: Relation plus ship: a relation that is kept like a ship at sea.
normal.cn: relation 加 ship：像船在海上一样被维持的 relation。

normal.en: A working relationship is built, not found.
normal.cn: a working relationship 是建起来的，不是捡到的。

normal.en: A relationship between figures is a pattern, not a person.
normal.cn: 数字之间的关系是一种模式，不是人。

normal.en: In a relationship means the couple is committed.
normal.cn: in a relationship 指两人已经在交往。

normal.en: The ship in relationship is a suffix of state, not a boat.
normal.cn: relationship 里的 ship 是表状态的后缀，不是船。

abstract.en: A relationship is a bridge that both ends must repair.
abstract.cn: 关系是一座两端都得修桥的桥。

abstract.en: What is not maintained quietly returns to being two strangers.
abstract.cn: 不维系的东西，会悄悄退回成两个陌生人。

abstract.en: The quality of a life is largely the quality of its relationships.
abstract.cn: 生活的质地，很大程度上是关系的质地。

examples.en: They built a working relationship over ten years.
examples.cn: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。

examples.en: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
examples.cn: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。

dict_mnemonic.text: relation（关系）加 ship（状态）：不是画一条线，而是长期维持这种状态，就是 relationship。

root: 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 英语 relation ＋ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态）→ relationship；同族有 relate、relation、relative、related，词干出自拉丁 ferre（携带）。

definition_zh: 大门；登机口；闸门；（比喻）通道
definition_en: a movable barrier closing an opening in a fence or wall, or an airport exit to a plane
core_image: 一扇可开合的木门横在篱笆缺口处，锁链垂在门柱上
scene: 候机厅广播响了第三遍。 Passengers for flight eight six two gathered at gate fifteen.
sceneCN: 这里 gate 是「登机口」（第 3 个义项：机场登机通道口）；句意为862次航班的旅客聚集在15号登机口。

senses.title: A movable barrier in a fence or wall
senses.definition: a hinged or sliding barrier closing an opening in a wall or fence
senses.definitionCN: 装在墙或篱笆开口处、可开合的挡板
senses.example: The garden gate creaked in the north wind.
senses.exampleCN: 花园大门在北风里吱呀作响。
senses.why: The word names the physical barrier itself, the oldest and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名挡板本身，是最古老、居于中心的义项。

senses.title: A passage or entrance controlled by it
senses.definition: the opening or way that the barrier controls
senses.definitionCN: 由挡板控制的开口或通路
senses.example: Cattle funnel through the gate one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 牛一头一头地穿过栅门。
senses.why: The barrier and its opening blur into one label, since naming one names the passage.
senses.whyCN: 挡板与开口在命名上融为一体，叫出其一即指向通路。

senses.title: An airport exit to a plane
senses.definition: the numbered airport doorway leading passengers to a plane
senses.definitionCN: 机场内编号的旅客登机通道口
senses.example: Boarding starts forty minutes before at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 登机前四十分钟在登机口开始。
senses.why: Airports reused the controlled-passage idea, numbering each doorway like a gate.
senses.whyCN: 机场复用「受控通道」的观念，给每个出入口编号如门。

senses.title: A mechanical or water barrier
senses.definition: a sliding barrier controlling water, electrons, or traffic
senses.definitionCN: 控制水流、电流或车流的滑动挡板
senses.example: The sluice gate lifted and the mill wheel turned.
senses.exampleCN: 水闸升起，磨坊水轮转动起来。
senses.why: The same barrier shape works for water and circuits, so the engineering sense borrowed it.
senses.whyCN: 同一种挡板形状适用于水流与电路，工程义项由此借用。

senses.title: Metaphorical opening to progress
senses.definition: a figurative entry point to a stage, career, or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 通往某一阶段、职业或知识的比喻性入口
senses.example: Learning to read is the gate to every other subject.
senses.exampleCN: 学会阅读是通往其他所有学科之门。
senses.why: Where one passes from outside to inside, speech opens a gate, borrowing the physical image.
senses.whyCN: 凡是从外到内的跨越，言语都会开启一扇门，借用实体画面。

senses.title: To restrict access by barriers
senses.definition: to fit with a gate or limit who may pass, as gated community
senses.definitionCN: 安装门禁或限制谁可通行，如 gated community
senses.example: The lane is gated after ten at night.
senses.exampleCN: 这条巷子每晚十点后上闸。
senses.why: The noun moved into the verb slot as access control became an everyday practice.
senses.whyCN: 随着门禁成为日常，名词滑入了动词位置。

intro.en: Gate is a native Norse-influenced word for a barrier, distinct from the northern gate meaning street.
intro.cn: gate 是受诺斯语影响的「门闩」本土词，与北方方言里表示「街道」的 gate 是两回事。

items.en: Old Norse gata meant an opening, passage, or road.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gata 意为开口、通道、道路。

items.en: Old English geat meant a gate or opening in an enclosure.
items.cn: 古英语 geat 指围栏上的门或开口。

items.en: Scandinavian settlement reinforced both the road and the barrier senses in England.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚人的定居使「街道」与「门闩」两义在英格兰并存。

items.en: Middle English gate kept the barrier sense while street uses survived in place names.
items.cn: 中古英语 gate 保留门闩义，街道义留存于地名之中。

items.en: Modern English added airports, sluices, verbs, and metaphor.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了机场、水闸、动词与比喻用法。

note.en: Gate pairs with door, fence, and gatecrash; in place names it may mean street itself.
note.cn: gate 与 door、fence、gatecrash 成套出现；在地名中它可能意指街道本身。

normal.en: Airport gate numbers follow boarding order.

normal.en: A gated community is a neighbourhood locked by gates.

abstract.en: Hinge, post, chain: the moving triangle of every gate.

abstract.en: Passing a gate feels like crossing into a new chapter.

abstract.en: Water pushing against a sluice gate is power held back.

examples.cn: 他把自行车停在花园大门外。

examples.en: The gate for flight two one nine is changing.
examples.cn: 219次航班的登机口有变动。

examples.en: They gated the alley to stop theft.
examples.cn: 他们给小巷装了门禁以防盗窃。

definition_zh: 简单的；朴素的；单纯的

senses.example: This question is simple.

definition_zh: 目标；目的；球门；进球得分；终点
definition_en: the end point you aim at, whether a line to cross, a result to achieve, or a frame to put the ball into
core_image: 跑道尽头插着的一面旗，所有脚步都朝它收拢
scene: 决赛的最后时刻，前锋一脚把球踢进了球门。 She scored the winning goal in the last minute of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 goal 是「进球、得分」（第 4 个义项：把球送进球门所得到的一分）；句意：她在比赛最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。场景要点：球门网、飞过门线的球、停在最后一分钟的计时器，以及看台上举起的手臂。

senses.title: The end point of a race
senses.definition: the mark or line at which a race ends
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑结束处的标记或界线
senses.example: The runners sprinted toward the goal at the far end of the track.
senses.exampleCN: 选手们朝跑道尽头的终点冲刺。
senses.why: Goal is first recorded in the 1530s as the end point of a race. The word names the mark that ends motion, and its own origin is not settled.
senses.whyCN: goal 最早在 16 世纪 30 年代记录为赛跑的终点。这个词命名的是让运动结束的那个标记，而它自身的来源尚无定论。

senses.title: The object of an effort
senses.definition: the result or state that a person or group works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体努力要达成的结果或状态
senses.example: Her goal is to finish the marathon under four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目标是在四小时内跑完马拉松。
senses.why: The figurative sense, also from the 1540s, treats life as a course: the result you want is the mark you run toward.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻义同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代：它把人生当作一段赛程，你想要的结果就是你朝它奔跑的那个标记。

senses.title: The frame where the ball is put
senses.definition: the structure of posts and net into which players try to send the ball
senses.definitionCN: 由门柱和球网构成、球员努力把球送进去的结构
senses.example: The goalkeeper stood between the posts of the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员站在球门柱之间。
senses.why: The sports sense, also from the 1540s, makes the end point physical: a frame marks the place where the ball must arrive.
senses.whyCN: 同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代的体育义项，把终点变成实物：一个框架标出了球必须抵达的位置。

senses.title: A score made in the frame
senses.definition: a point gained by sending the ball through or into the goal
senses.definitionCN: 把球送过门线或送进球门而得到的一分
senses.example: She scored the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。
senses.why: By metonymy the frame gives its name to the event of putting the ball through it: the endpoint becomes the point gained.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，框架把自己的名字借给了“把球送进去”这件事：终点变成了所得的一分。

senses.title: A measured target in work
senses.definition: a figure or quota that a team or company is expected to reach
senses.definitionCN: 团队或公司被要求达到的数字或定额
senses.example: The sales team missed its quarterly goal by two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 销售团队以两个百分点的差距未能达到季度指标。
senses.why: A number can serve as the mark: once the target is measurable, the race endpoint becomes a quota.
senses.whyCN: 数字也可以充当那个标记：一旦目标可以计量，赛跑的终点就变成了定额。

senses.title: A long-term aim in life
senses.definition: a distant aim that gives direction to a person's life or career
senses.definitionCN: 为人生或事业提供方向的远期追求
senses.example: His goal is to run a clinic in his home town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的志向是在家乡开一家诊所。
senses.why: The largest version of the same image: a whole life is the course, and one distant mark gives it direction.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一个意象的最大版本：整个人生是赛程，一个远处的标记为它提供方向。

senses.title: Own goal: a score against your own side
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase own goal, a goal scored accidentally for the opposing team
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配 own goal 中，指误为对方球队打进的一球
senses.example: The defender's own goal decided the tie.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫的乌龙球决定了这场平局的结果。
senses.why: The frame is neutral: a ball put into the wrong one still counts. English names that accident with the fixed phrase own goal.
senses.whyCN: 球门本身是中立的：球进了错误的那一个，仍然算数。英语用固定说法 own goal 命名这种意外。

senses.title: Goal line and goal area
senses.definition: the line and the marked area on the field that belong to the goal
senses.definitionCN: 场地上属于球门的那条线和被划出的区域
senses.example: The ball crossed the goal line by a few centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 球越过球门线几厘米。
senses.why: The frame projects a boundary onto the field; the line and the area are the ground version of the same endpoint.
senses.whyCN: 球门把一条边界投射到场地上；球门线与球门区是同一个终点在地面上的版本。

senses.title: Attributive: goal-directed, goal-setting
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe activity organised around a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词之前，描述围绕目标组织起来的活动
senses.example: Goal-setting theory treats clear targets as a motivator.
senses.exampleCN: 目标设定理论把清晰的目标视为一种激励因素。
senses.why: When the word moves in front of another noun, it stops naming a mark and starts labelling the activity that is organised around one.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词移到另一个名词前面时，它不再命名一个标记，而是给围绕某个标记组织起来的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is a single noun of uncertain origin: it appears in the 1530s as the end of a race, and every later sense keeps that 'mark ahead' shape.
intro.cn: goal 是一个来源不确定的单词：它在 16 世纪 30 年代以“赛跑终点”出现，后来每个义项都保留着“前方有一个标记”的形状。

items.en: First recorded as 'end point of a race'. The word appears once earlier, as gol in an early-14c poem, with an apparent sense of 'boundary, limit'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“赛跑的终点”。这个词更早还出现过一次，在 14 世纪早期的一首诗里写作 gol，似乎是“边界、界限”的意思。

items.en: Three origins have been proposed and none is established: Old English *gal 'obstacle, barrier', implied by gælan 'to hinder' and by compounds such as singal and widgal; Old Norse geil 'a narrow glen, a passage'; or Old French gaule 'long pole, stake', which is Germanic in origin. The source is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 先后有三种来源被提出，但没有一种得到确认：一是古英语 *gal“障碍、壁垒”，由 gælan“阻碍”以及 singal、widgal 等复合词推知；二是古诺尔斯语 geil“狭窄峡谷、通道”；三是古法语 gaule“长杆、桩”，而后者本身出自日耳曼语。词源属于存疑。

items.en: The sports sense 'place where the ball is put to score' is recorded, and in the same decade the figurative sense 'object of an effort'.
items.cn: 记录到体育义“把球放进去得分的位置”，同一时期还出现比喻义“努力的目标”。

items.en: Goal-keeper appears in the 1650s; field goal in 1889; goal-tender in 1889; goalie in 1921 as a shortening of goal-tender.
items.cn: goal-keeper 出现于 17 世纪 50 年代；field goal 与 goal-tender 出现于 1889 年；goalie 于 1921 年作为 goal-tender 的缩略形式出现。

items.en: Goalpost, goal line, goal area, own goal and goalless fill out the family. Goal itself remains a noun only; there is no verb 'to goal' in standard English.
items.cn: goalpost、goal line、goal area、own goal、goalless 补全了这一词族。goal 本身始终只是名词；标准英语中没有 to goal 这样的动词用法。

items.en: Gold is a different word with a different history; the resemblance to goal is only in sound and spelling. German Ziel means 'goal, target' but is not the source of the English word.
items.cn: gold 是另一个词，来历完全不同；它与 goal 的相似只在读音和拼写上。德语 Ziel 意为“目标、终点”，但它并不是英语这个词的来源。

note.en: The first group is sound and spelling neighbours, including two that merely look like goal; the second compares the words for what you are trying to reach.
note.cn: 第一组是读音与拼写上的邻居，其中两个只是看起来像 goal；第二组比较表示“你想要抵达的东西”的几个词。

entries.definition: the yellow metal. It has no historical link with goal; only the vowel and the final consonant resemble each other.
entries.definitionCN: 那种黄色金属。它与 goal 没有任何历史联系，只是元音和结尾辅音相近。

entries.definition: one of the two uprights of a goal. It is a compound of goal plus post, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 球门两根立柱之一。它是 goal 加 post 的合成词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a goalkeeper. It is a 1921 shortening of goal-tender, so it belongs to the goal family.
entries.definitionCN: 守门员。它是 1921 年对 goal-tender 的缩略，因此属于 goal 词族。

entries.definition: without a goal being scored, as in a goalless draw. The suffix -less marks absence, not a new sense.
entries.definitionCN: 没有进球的，如 goalless draw。后缀 -less 标记“没有”，并不产生新义项。

entries.definition: what you intend to achieve; also the act of pointing at something. It is close to goal but often more personal and less measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 你打算达成的东西；也指瞄准的动作。它与 goal 接近，但往往更个人化、更不可量化。

entries.definition: a specific result that an organisation formally sets out to achieve. It is more formal and more measurable than goal.
entries.definitionCN: 组织正式设定要达成的具体结果。它比 goal 更正式、更可量化。

entries.definition: a level or figure to be reached, often with a deadline. It stresses the number to hit, while goal stresses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 需要达到的水平或数字，常带截止时间。它强调要命中的数字，而 goal 强调方向。

entries.definition: the reason something exists or is done. It answers 'why', while goal answers 'where to'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或被做的理由。它回答“为什么”，而 goal 回答“往哪里去”。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts and real relatives: the noun goal, its compounds goalpost and goalkeeper, and the 1921 shortening goalie.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构词成分与真实同族词：名词 goal，它的合成词 goalpost、goalkeeper，以及 1921 年的缩略形式 goalie。

normal.en: Goal first meant the end of a race: a mark you run toward.
normal.cn: goal 最初指赛跑的终点：一个你朝它奔跑的标记。

normal.en: The sports frame is that same mark made visible, and the score is named after the frame.
normal.cn: 体育中的球门就是同一个标记变成实物，而“得分”又被球门命名。

normal.en: Gold and goal are only neighbours in sound; they have no shared history.
normal.cn: gold 与 goal 只是读音上的邻居，没有共同的来历。

normal.en: Own goal is a fixed phrase: the ball goes into the frame, but the wrong one.
normal.cn: own goal 是固定说法：球确实进了门，只是进错了那一个。

normal.en: Goal-setting and goal-directed show the noun working as a modifier, common in psychology and management.
normal.cn: goal-setting 与 goal-directed 显示这个名词可以作修饰语，这在心理学与管理学中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a flag at the end of a track: every lane converges on it.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道尽头插着一面旗：每一条跑道都朝它收拢。

abstract.en: The flag can be a line, a number, a frame or a distant plan; the word always points to one mark.
abstract.cn: 那面旗可以是一条线、一个数字、一个框架，或一个远期的计划；这个词始终指向同一个标记。

abstract.en: A goal is not the running; it is the place where the running stops being open.
abstract.cn: 目标不是奔跑本身；它是奔跑不再敞开的那一点。

examples.en: The team's goal is to cut water use by a third within five years.
examples.cn: 这个团队的目标是在五年内把用水量削减三分之一。

examples.en: He scored twice and set up the third goal.
examples.cn: 他打进两球，并助攻了第三个进球。

examples.en: Without a clear goal, the meetings drifted from topic to topic.
examples.cn: 没有明确的目标，会议就从一个话题漂到另一个话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “够儿”——一路跑到尽头，够着那面旗儿 → goal 目标、终点（只借音，不表词源）

root: 词源存疑：最早指赛跑的终点（1530 年代），可能来自古英语表示“障碍、界限”的词或古法语“长杆”；核心是“所有努力都朝向的那个终点”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of goal, all built on one position: a mark placed ahead, which motion or effort is organised to reach.
sensesIntro.cn: goal 的九个义项都建立在同一个位置关系上：前方放着一个标记，运动或努力都围绕抵达它来组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark ahead that every step converges on.
core.cn: 核心意象：前方的一个标记，所有脚步都朝它收拢。

branches.en: RACE: the original sense is the physical end point of a course.
branches.cn: 赛跑：最初的义项就是赛程的物理终点。

branches.en: AIM: the mark becomes mental, from a single task to a whole life's direction.
branches.cn: 目标：标记变成心里的，从一项任务一直到整个人生的方向。

branches.en: FRAME: in sport the mark is built of posts and line, a place the ball must reach.
branches.cn: 球门：在体育中，标记由门柱与门线构成，是球必须抵达的位置。

branches.en: SCORE: the frame lends its name to the point, including the accidental own goal.
branches.cn: 得分：球门把名字借给那一分，也包括意外的乌龙球。

branches.en: MEASURE: a number can be the mark, and the noun can label activity organised around it.
branches.cn: 计量：数字可以成为标记，这个名词也能给围绕标记组织的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is not built from prefixes or suffixes; it is one noun whose family is made of compounds and a few endings such as -ie, -less and the plural -s.
intro.cn: goal 不是由前缀或后缀构成的；它是一个单词名词，其词族由合成词和 -ie、-less、复数 -s 等少数词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is known. The word appears in English in the 1530s with an uncertain origin, and the three candidates are Old English, Old Norse and Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有已知的拉丁语来源。这个词在 16 世纪 30 年代出现于英语，来源不确定，三个候选分别来自古英语、古诺尔斯语与古法语。

items.meaning: an end point, aim, or frame for scoring
items.example: The goal is to finish before noon.
items.exampleCN: 目标是在中午之前完成。

items.meaningCN: 多个目标；多个进球（复数）
items.example: The team has scored nine goals this season.
items.exampleCN: 这支球队本赛季已打进九球。

items.meaningCN: 没有进球的（-less 表示“没有”）
守门员（-ie 构成亲昵缩略）

items.meaning: the player who guards the goal
items.example: The goalkeeper punched the ball clear.

items.meaning: one of the uprights of a goal

items.example: The ball rolled over the goal line.

items.meaning: the marked area in front of the goal
items.example: The foul happened inside the goal area.
items.exampleCN: 那次犯规发生在球门区内。

items.meaning: a goal scored accidentally against one's own team
items.example: His own goal put the visitors ahead.
items.exampleCN: 他的乌龙球让客队领先。

items.meaning: a score made from the playing field, as in football
items.meaningCN: 射门得分（美式足球等的场上得分）
items.example: They won with a field goal in the final seconds.
items.exampleCN: 他们在最后几秒靠一次射门得分赢下比赛。

definition_zh: 海岸；海滨；（沿特定方向的）滑行
definition_en: the land beside the sea; to move without using power
core_image: 大海与陆地相遇的那条长长的线
scene: 暑假，全家坐车去看蓝色的大海。 We drove to the coast for the summer holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 coast 是「海岸；海滨」（第 1 个义项：陆地与海相接的地带）；句意是我们开车去海边过暑假。

derivatives.zh: 由 coast 加后缀 -al 构成，义为「沿海的；海岸的」
由 coast 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「沿海航行船；杯垫；过山车（roller coaster）」

senses.title: The land along the sea
senses.definition: the land next to the sea
senses.definitionCN: 紧靠大海的陆地
senses.example: Fishing boats leave the coast before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船天亮前就离开了海岸。
senses.why: The sea never walks inland, so where it stops, the coast begins.
senses.whyCN: 大海从不深入内陆，它停下的地方就是海岸。

senses.title: To slide without power
senses.definition: to move forward without using the engine or pedalling
senses.definitionCN: 不借助发动机或蹬踏而前进
senses.example: The bike coasted down the long hill.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车顺着长坡滑了下去。
senses.why: A sled on ice needs no push once it starts, like a boat carried by the sea.
senses.whyCN: 冰上的雪橇一旦滑动便无需再推，正如被海托着的船。

senses.title: To do something without effort
senses.definition: to progress easily without real effort
senses.definitionCN: 不费力气地顺利推进
senses.example: He coasted through the easy test.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松通过了这场容易的考试。
senses.why: Smooth motion without pushing feels like sliding downhill, so easy work is called coasting.
senses.whyCN: 无需用力便顺利前进，如同顺坡下滑，轻松过关便叫 coasting。

intro.en: Coast began as a rib, then became a side, and finally the side of the land.
intro.cn: coast 起初是「肋骨」，后来变成「侧面」，最终成了陆地的边缘。

items.en: Latin costa meant a rib or the side of anything.
items.cn: 拉丁语 costa 指肋骨，或物体的侧面。

items.en: Old French coste kept the sense of a side or slope.
items.cn: 古法语 coste 保留「侧面；坡」的意思。

items.en: Middle English coast first meant any side or border, even of a room.
items.cn: 中古英语 coast 最初泛指任何边界，甚至房间的边。

items.en: The sea border became the main sense in Modern English.
items.cn: 现代英语中海陆边界成了主要义项。

items.en: The gliding sense grew from ships carried smoothly along the coast.
items.cn: 滑行义来自船沿海岸被海平稳地带着走。

note.en: The first group collects the coast family; the second collects seaside and slide words.
note.cn: 第一组收 coast 词族，第二组收海边与滑行类词。

entries.definition: Near or belonging to the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沿海的」，由 coast 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A ship sailing near the coast; a roller coaster.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沿海船；过山车（roller coaster）」，由 coast 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The price of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「价格」，与 coast 仅一字母之差，词源无关。

entries.definition: The land along any water, narrower than coast.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「岸」，泛指任何水域的岸。

entries.definition: A sandy or stony seaside area.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海滩」，指海岸的沙滩部分。

entries.definition: The coast as a holiday place.

normalIntro.en: Remember coast through its rib root and its gliding ship.
normalIntro.cn: 借「肋骨」词根与顺海滑行的船记忆 coast。

normal.en: coast comes from Latin costa, a rib.
normal.cn: coast 来自拉丁语 costa（肋骨）。

normal.en: coastal means near the sea.
normal.cn: coastal 指沿海的。

normal.en: coast guard protects people at sea.
normal.cn: coast guard 保护海上的人。

normal.en: the bike coasted down the hill.
normal.cn: 自行车顺坡滑下。

normal.en: a roller coaster runs on high tracks.
normal.cn: roller coaster 在高空轨道上跑。

abstract.en: Hear soft waves folding over wet sand all afternoon.
abstract.cn: 听一下午海浪在湿沙上轻轻翻卷。

abstract.en: Feel the wind push your face as the bike rolls downhill.
abstract.cn: 感受自行车下滑时风扑在脸上。

abstract.en: See a map line where blue meets yellow.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上蓝与黄相接的那条线。

examples.en: The coast near our city has tall cliffs and cold wind.
examples.cn: 我们城市附近的海岸有高高的悬崖和冷风。

examples.en: We coasted down the hill and saved half the ride.
examples.cn: 我们顺坡滑下去，省了一半路程。

examples.en: The coast guard saved two swimmers yesterday.
examples.cn: 昨天海岸警卫队救了两名游泳者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「寇斯特」——海风「寇」不去的海「斯特」（side 侧），coast 就是大陆的侧边。

root: 拉丁语 costa（肋骨；侧面）→ 古法语 coste（侧；坡）→ 中古英语 coast（边界）→ 现代英语「海岸」并引申出「滑行」；同族词有 intercostal（肋间的），派生词有 coastal（沿海的）、coaster（沿海船）。

sensesIntro.en: Coast draws the line where sea meets land, then borrows smooth sliding.
sensesIntro.cn: coast 画出海陆相接的线，又借来顺坡的滑行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the long line where the sea stops and land begins
core.cn: 核心意象：海停下、陆地开始的那条长线

branches.en: The sea border of land
Sliding without power
Effortless progress
Boats, cliffs and tides
Riding an easy slope

intro.en: Coast sends out two simple derivatives and meets its relatives.
intro.cn: coast 派生出两个简单派生词，并会见它的亲戚们。

latinIntro.en: Latin costa, a rib, is the root hiding inside coast.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 costa（肋骨）是藏在 coast 里的词根。

items.example: The coastal town lives on fishing.
items.exampleCN: 这座沿海小镇靠捕鱼为生。

items.meaning: a coasting ship; a roller coaster

items.example: We built castles on the beach.
The seaside town is busy in July.
items.exampleCN: 七月的海边小镇很热闹。

items.example: The slope was too steep to cycle.

definition_zh: 英寸；少量；缓慢移动
definition_en: a unit of length equal to 2.54 centimeters, or to move very slowly
core_image: 尺子上最小的一格，一寸一寸挪
scene: 木工房里拉卷尺。 The carpenter measured the shelf to the last inch.
sceneCN: 这里 inch 是「英寸」（第 1 个义项：长度单位）；句意：木匠把书架量到了最后一英寸。

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a unit of length, 2.54 centimeters
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，2.54 厘米
senses.example: The screen measures twenty inches across.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕对角线长二十英寸。
senses.why: The thumb joint of the old ruler: the smallest named step.
senses.whyCN: 旧尺上的拇指关节：最小的命名刻度。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a very small distance or degree
senses.definitionCN: 极小的距离或程度
senses.example: The bullet missed him by an inch.
senses.exampleCN: 子弹差一寸就打中他。
senses.why: One smallest step decides a whole outcome.
senses.whyCN: 最小的一步决定整个结局。

senses.title: To move very slowly
senses.definition: to move slowly and by small degrees
senses.definitionCN: 以极小的步幅缓慢移动
senses.example: The truck inched through the narrow gate.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车缓缓挤过窄门。
senses.why: The unit becomes a verb: advance one smallest step at a time.
senses.whyCN: 单位转动词：一次只挪最小的一步。

senses.title: Rainfall or snowfall measure
senses.definition: a unit for measuring rain or snow depth
senses.definitionCN: 测量降雨或积雪深度的单位
senses.example: Three inches of snow fell overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜下了三英寸厚的雪。
senses.why: The ruler is lifted from wood to weather.
senses.whyCN: 尺子从木工活被举到天气里。

senses.title: Every inch: completely
senses.definition: in every respect; completely
senses.definitionCN: 在每个方面；完全地
senses.example: She looked every inch a captain.
senses.exampleCN: 她看上去完全是个船长。
senses.why: Every smallest step of the ruler adds up to the whole picture.
senses.whyCN: 尺上每一小格加起来就是全貌。

intro.en: Inch comes from Old English ynce, borrowed from Latin uncia, a twelfth, the twelfth part of a Roman foot. The same Latin word gave English ounce; inch and ounce are twins.
intro.cn: inch 来自古英语 ynce，借自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」，即罗马尺的十二分之一。同一个词也给了英语 ounce；inch 与 ounce 是孪生词。

items.en: Latin uncia meant a twelfth part, of a foot or of a pound.
items.cn: 拉丁语 uncia 指十二分之一，或指尺或磅。

items.en: The twelfth of a pound became the ounce; the twelfth of a foot became the inch.
items.cn: 一磅的十二分之一成了盎司；一尺的十二分之一成了英寸。

items.en: Old English ynce fixed the borrowing; the inch then matched three barleycorns laid end to end.
items.cn: 古英语 ynce 定型借词；当时的英寸相当于三粒大麦首尾相接。

items.en: Middle English inch settled the spelling and grew the small-amount sense.
items.cn: 中古英语定型拼写，发展出少量义。

items.en: In nineteen fifty-nine the inch was fixed internationally at exactly 2.54 centimeters.
items.cn: 一九五九年英寸在国际上被定为精确的 2.54 厘米。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the inch family and its twin ounce. The meaning group compares small units and small movements.
note.cn: 形近组收录 inch 词族及其孪生词 ounce；词义组比较小单位与小移动。

entries.definition: a unit of weight, from the same Latin uncia.
entries.definitionCN: 盎司。出自同一个拉丁词 uncia。

entries.definition: plural of inch.
a feeling that makes you scratch. One letter apart.
the metric small step; one inch is 2.54 of them.
entries.definitionCN: 厘米。公制的小格；1 英寸等于 2.54 厘米。

entries.definition: to move slowly and quietly, close to the verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢潜行。接近动词义项。

entries.definition: a tiny amount or part.

normalIntro.en: These hooks link inch and ounce, use inch by inch and flag the itch trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 inch 与 ounce 相连，用 inch by inch，并标记 itch 陷阱。

normal.en: inch and ounce are twins: both from Latin uncia, a twelfth.
normal.cn: inch 与 ounce 是孪生词：都来自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」。

normal.en: inch by inch is the classic patience phrase.
normal.cn: inch by inch 是经典的耐心短语。

normal.en: The verb inched shows tiny progress: the truck inched forward.
normal.cn: 动词 inched 表现微小进展：卡车缓缓前行。

normal.en: Every inch a leader means completely a leader.
normal.cn: every inch a leader 意为彻头彻尾的领袖。

normal.en: Do not mix inch and itch: one measures, one scratches.
normal.cn: 别混淆 inch 与 itch：一个测量，一个挠痒。

abstract.en: One image: a thumb pressing the smallest mark on a ruler.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：拇指按在尺上最小的一格。

abstract.en: An inch is the step between fail and triumph.

abstract.en: Slow verbs love this word: inch, creep, edge.

examples.en: They won by inches in the final seconds.
examples.cn: 最后几秒他们以毫厘之差获胜。

sensesIntro.en: Inch is the smallest ruler step: a length, a near-miss, a slow crawl, a rainfall measure, and the whole when every step is counted.
sensesIntro.cn: inch 是尺上最小的格：一段长度、一次险胜、一次缓行、一份降水量，以及每格都数时的全部。

core.en: The smallest named step on the ruler of distance, effort and outcome.
core.cn: 距离、努力与结局之尺上最小的命名刻度。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示那个分裂为英寸与盎司的「十二分之一」名词。

definition_zh: 金色的；金黄的；黄金般的；极好的；重要的（黄金时代）
definition_en: of the colour or quality of gold, or precious and outstanding
core_image: 铺满金光：像黄金一样又亮又贵重
scene: 秋天的午后，稻田铺成了一片金黄。 The children ran across the golden field after school.
sceneCN: 这里 golden 是「金色的」（第 1 个义项：像黄金的颜色）；句意为放学后孩子们跑过金色的田野。

pos.zh: 金色的；黄金的；宝贵的；兴盛的

senses.title: Of the colour of gold
senses.definition: bright yellow in colour like gold
senses.definitionCN: 像黄金般的明亮黄色
senses.example: The children ran across the golden field after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后孩子们跑过金色的田野。
senses.why: The colour of the metal is painted onto hair, fields and sand.
senses.whyCN: 金属的颜色被刷到头发、田野与沙滩上。

senses.title: Made of solid gold
senses.definition: made of real gold
senses.definitionCN: 用真金制成
senses.example: She kept her golden necklace in a velvet box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把金项链收在天鹅绒盒子里。
senses.why: When the metal itself forms the thing, the -en adjective names the material.
senses.whyCN: 当金属本身构成物件，-en 形容词便指材料。

senses.title: Precious and excellent
senses.definition: outstandingly good and valuable, as in a golden opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 格外优秀且宝贵，如绝佳的机会
senses.example: This is a golden opportunity to learn from the master.
senses.exampleCN: 这是向大师学习的绝佳机会。
senses.why: Gold was always the most precious metal, so chances as precious as gold are golden.
senses.whyCN: 金历来最贵重，于是像金一样难得的机会便是 golden。

senses.title: Prosperous and flourishing
senses.definition: marked by prosperity and success, as in the golden age
senses.definitionCN: 以繁荣成功为标志，如黄金时代
senses.example: People still look back on the golden age of the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 人们仍在怀念剧场的黄金时代。
senses.why: The best years shine like gold, so flourishing times take the golden name.
senses.whyCN: 最好的岁月像金子一样发光，繁盛时代便得到 golden 之名。

senses.title: Fiftieth anniversary
senses.definition: relating to a fiftieth anniversary, as in a golden wedding
senses.definitionCN: 与五十周年纪念相关，如金婚
senses.example: They held a golden wedding party after fifty years together.
senses.exampleCN: 共同生活五十年后他们举办了金婚派对。
senses.why: Fifty years together are as rare and precious as gold.
senses.whyCN: 相伴五十年稀有如金，纪念日便以金为名。

intro.en: Golden is gold with the old adjective ending -en added on.
intro.cn: golden 就是 gold 加上古英语形容词后缀 -en。

items.en: Old English gylden was formed from gold with the -en ending.
items.cn: 古英语 gylden 由 gold 加 -en 后缀构成。

items.en: The Germanic -in suffix formed material adjectives like wooden and waxen.
items.cn: 日耳曼 -in 后缀构成材料类形容词，如 wooden 与 waxen。

items.en: Middle English gylden simplified to golden and widened to the colour sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 gylden 简化为 golden，并扩展出颜色义。

items.en: The precious-chance sense grew beside the colour sense in the same period.
items.cn: 宝贵机会义与颜色义同期生长。

items.en: Modern English kept golden for colour, material, quality and anniversaries.
items.cn: 现代英语的 golden 兼指颜色、材料、品质与周年纪念。

note.en: The words below resemble golden in form or in preciousness.
note.cn: 以下词与 golden 形近，或同属贵重义场。

entries.definition: Shining warmly with colour or praise.

abstract.en: See long fair hair catching the sun on a windy day.
abstract.cn: 想象大风天里金色长发迎着阳光。

abstract.en: Think of a rare door opening once and closing forever.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇难得的门只开一次便永远关闭。

definition_zh: 发展；开发；成长；新动态
definition_en: the process of growing or changing into a better or bigger form; a new event
core_image: 从草图到大楼一点点长高的工地
scene: 校门口那块空地围了起来，公告牌写着新图书馆工程。 The development of the new library will finish next autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 development 是「开发、建设」（第 2 个义项：具体的开发项目）；句意是新图书馆的建设将于明年秋天完工。

collocations.zh: 一个新进展；新建开发区

由 develop 加 -ing 构成，义为「发展中的」

senses.title: The process of growing or improving
senses.definition: the process of becoming bigger, better or more complete
senses.definitionCN: 变得更大、更好或更完整的过程
senses.example: The development of her drawing skill took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 她绘画技能的成长花了三年。
senses.why: Unfolding takes time, and the finished process needs its own name.
senses.whyCN: 展开需要时间，这个完整的过程需要专属的名字，便是 development。

senses.title: A new building or project
senses.definition: a group of new buildings or an area being built
senses.definitionCN: 新建的楼群或正在建设的区域
senses.example: A quiet housing development stands where the farm used to be.
senses.exampleCN: 农场原址上矗立着一片安静的住宅新区。
senses.why: What developers build was named after the act of developing.
senses.whyCN: 开发商开发出来的成果便以「开发」这一行为命名。

senses.title: A new event or change
senses.definition: a new event that changes a situation
senses.definitionCN: 改变局面的事件或变化
senses.example: The early goal was an unexpected development in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 开场进球是比赛中出乎意料的新变化。
senses.why: A situation also unfolds, and each new turn is one development.
senses.whyCN: 局势也在不断展开，每一次新的转折就是一个 development。

intro.en: Development is the noun of develop, keeping the unfolding idea.
intro.cn: development 是 develop 的名词，保留了「展开」的意思。

items.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为滚动；dis- 增加展开之意。

items.en: French developpement carried the word into formal writing.
items.cn: 法语 developpement 把这个词带入正式书面语。

items.en: English formed development with the noun ending -ment.
items.cn: 英语用名词后缀 -ment 构成 development。

items.en: Science and industry used it for growth processes of all kinds.
items.cn: 科学与工业用它指各种生长过程。

items.en: City building gave it the sense of a new housing or business project.
items.cn: 城市建设赋予它住宅或商业开发项目的含义。

note.en: These words share the develop family or describe growth and change.

examples.en: The teacher praised the steady development of my handwriting.
examples.cn: 老师称赞我书写能力的稳步进步。

examples.en: Every match brings new developments, so plans must change.
examples.cn: 每场比赛都有新变化，所以计划也要调整。

examples.en: The park's development includes a small library for children.
examples.cn: 公园的规划中包含一座儿童小图书馆。
