definition_zh: 奖品；奖赏；可贵之物；珍视；获奖的
definition_en: something given to the winner of a contest; something valuable that is worth striving for; to value something highly; and, before a noun, award-winning or of outstanding quality
core_image: 人群中高高举起的一只银杯
scene: 礼堂里坐满了人，主持人念出名字的一刻，后排的女孩愣了一下才站起来。 The girl walked to the front to collect her prize while the whole hall clapped.
sceneCN: 这里的 prize 是「奖品」（第 1 个义项：比赛或评比中发给获胜者的东西）；句意为全场鼓掌时，女孩走到台前领取奖品。图中可辨识物件：礼堂座位、领奖台、银杯。

derivatives.zh: 由 prize（奖）与 fighter（打斗者）复合而成，义为「职业拳击手」
由 prize 与 winner 复合而成，义为「获奖者」

senses.title: Something given to the winner of a contest
senses.definition: an object, title, or sum of money given to the person who wins a competition or does something outstanding
senses.definitionCN: 发给比赛获胜者或表现突出者的物品、称号或奖金
senses.example: The first prize was a small silver cup.
senses.exampleCN: 一等奖是一只小银杯。
senses.why: The French source carried two meanings at once, cost and reward; English kept the reward half for what a winner carries away.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源同时带着代价与回报两层；英语把回报那一半留下来，用来指获胜者带走的东西。

senses.title: Something valuable that is worth striving for
senses.titleCN: 可贵之物；值得争取的目标
senses.definition: a thing or quality so valuable that people work hard to obtain or keep it
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵到人们愿意努力去获得或守住的东西或品质
senses.example: A quiet hour in the morning is the real prize of an early start.
senses.exampleCN: 早晨安静的一小时，才是早起真正的收获。
senses.why: Once a prize is what you get for effort, the word can name anything worth that effort, even something nobody can hand you.
senses.whyCN: 既然 prize 是努力之后得到的东西，这个词就能指任何值得那份努力的事物，哪怕没有人能把它递到你手上。

senses.title: To value something highly
senses.definition: to think that something is extremely valuable and to treat it with care
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物极为宝贵，因而小心对待
senses.example: She prizes the letters her grandmother wrote more than any jewellery.
senses.exampleCN: 比起任何首饰，她更珍视祖母写的那些信。
senses.why: The same French verb meant to set a price on and to esteem; English turned the second half into a verb of holding something dear.
senses.whyCN: 同一个法语动词既表示给某物定价，也表示看重；英语取了后一半，变成把某物看得珍贵的动词。

senses.title: Award-winning or of outstanding quality
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something that has won an award or is judged excellent
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，形容获得过奖项或被认为极为出色的东西
senses.example: The shop window was filled with prize vegetables from the village show.
senses.exampleCN: 橱窗里摆满了村里评比中获奖的蔬菜。
senses.why: Because a prize marks the best of a class, the noun moved in front of other nouns and became an adjective meaning top-grade.
senses.whyCN: 因为奖标记的是一类中最好的，这个名词就移到别的名词前面，变成表示头等的形容词。

intro.en: Prize and price are twins: both descend from Latin pretium, the word for worth, and only later did English split cost from reward.
intro.cn: prize 与 price 是一对双生词：两者都出自拉丁语 pretium（价值），英语后来才把代价与回报分开。

items.en: Pretium meant price, value, or worth, the amount at which a thing was valued, whether in coins or in esteem.
items.cn: pretium 意为价格、价值、所值，指一件东西被估出的分量，可以是用钱算的，也可以是用敬重算的。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed appretiare, to set a value on something, and this verb passed into French as the ordinary word for appraising.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语造出 appretiare，意为给某物估价，这个动词进入法语后成为平常说「评价」的词。

items.en: Old French pris meant both price and worth, and also the reward or honour given to a person who had done well.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 既指价格与价值，也指给表现优异者的回报或荣誉。

items.en: Middle English borrowed pris with both halves intact, so one word could speak of what a thing cost and of what a winner received.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 pris 时两半都还在，同一个词既能说一件东西值多少钱，也能说获胜者得到了什么。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the spellings settled apart: price kept cost, prize kept reward and the verb to value highly; the sense to force open belongs to a different word, Old French prise, a grasp.
items.cn: 十六世纪起两种拼写分家：price 守住代价，prize 守住回报以及珍视这个动词；而撬开一义属于另一个词，来自古法语 prise（抓住）。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the twin word and the shapes closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for awards and for things won.
note.cn: 形近组收那对双生词以及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示奖项与所得之物的词。

entries.definition: The amount of money a thing costs; it split from the same Latin pretium as prize.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所需的钱数；与 prize 同出拉丁语 pretium，后来分家。

entries.definition: To force something open with a lever, the British spelling of the American pry; a different word from Old French prise.
entries.definitionCN: 用杠杆撬开，是美式 pry 的英式拼写；与 prize 来源不同。

entries.definition: To express approval or admiration; it also goes back to Latin pretium, but through a French verb meaning to value.
entries.definitionCN: 表达赞许或钦佩；它也上溯到拉丁语 pretium，走的是意为「看重」的法语动词。

entries.definition: A person who fights for money in the ring; a compound of prize and fighter.
entries.definitionCN: 在拳台上为奖金而战的人；由 prize 与 fighter 复合而成。

entries.definition: Something given formally to recognise merit or a win.
entries.definitionCN: 为表彰功绩或胜利而正式发给的东西。

entries.definition: Something given in return for effort or good behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 因付出努力或表现良好而得到的回报。

entries.definition: An object kept as a symbol of a victory.
entries.definitionCN: 作为胜利象征而被保存的物件。

entries.definition: A flat piece of metal given to a winner or a hero.
entries.definitionCN: 发给获胜者或英雄的金属片。

normalIntro.en: The word shares a Latin ancestor with price, and its family keeps both halves of that ancestor: what a thing is worth, and what a person is worth to you.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与 price 共有一个拉丁祖先，它的同族保留了这个祖先的两半：一件东西值多少，以及一个人在你心里值多少。

normal.en: Pretium in Latin means worth, so prize began as a statement about value rather than about medals.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 意为价值，所以 prize 最初讲的是值多少，而不是奖牌。

normal.en: Price and prize are the same Latin word arriving twice: one kept the cost, the other kept the reward.
normal.cn: price 与 prize 是同一个拉丁词抵达两次：一个留下代价，一个留下回报。

normal.en: The verb prize, as in prize something highly, keeps the old sense of setting a value on a thing.
normal.cn: 动词 prize（如 prize something highly）保留的正是给某物估个高价的老意思。

normal.en: Prize before a noun, as in prize bull, works like an adjective: the animal that took the award.
normal.cn: prize 放在名词前（如 prize bull）就像形容词：拿过奖的那头牲口。

normal.en: The -prise in surprise comes from another word meaning a grasp, and it only looks like prize.
normal.cn: surprise 里的 -prise 来自另一个意为「抓住」的词，只是长得像 prize。

abstract.en: A single Latin word for worth grew two English faces, one asking what you pay and one asking what you win.
abstract.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁词长出两张英语面孔：一张问你付多少，一张问你赢什么。

abstract.en: A prize is worth made visible: a cup on a shelf turns an invisible judgement into an object you can hold.
abstract.cn: prize 是被看见的价值：架子上的一只杯子，把无形的评判变成可以拿在手里的东西。

abstract.en: To prize something is to put a price on it in the old sense, not to sell it but to admit it cannot be replaced.
abstract.cn: to prize 某物是用老意思给它标价，不是要卖掉它，而是承认它无可替代。

examples.en: The first prize was a small silver cup.
examples.cn: 一等奖是一只小银杯。

examples.en: She prizes the letters her grandmother wrote more than any jewellery.
examples.cn: 比起任何首饰，她更珍视祖母写的那些信。

examples.en: The girl walked to the front to collect her prize.
examples.cn: 女孩走到台前领取奖品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑来事」——好事扑过来，得了奖，就是 prize。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价值、价格）→ 口语拉丁语 appretiare（估价）→ 古法语 pris（价格；回报）→ 中古英语 pris → 现代英语分化为 price（价格）与 prize（奖品）。撬开一义另出古法语 prise（抓住），与前一支无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is worth; the senses divide into the reward a winner takes, the valuable thing worth working for, the act of valuing, and the adjective for what has won.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是价值；义项分成获胜者拿走的回报、值得为之努力的可贵之物、珍视的动作，以及形容获奖之物的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver cup lifted above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中高高举起的一只银杯。

branches.en: a cup raised at the front of a hall
branches.cn: 礼堂前方被举起的一只杯子

branches.en: a still morning hour that nobody can buy
branches.cn: 没人买得到的一段安静晨光

branches.en: a hand resting on an old bundle of letters
branches.cn: 一只手按在一叠旧信上

branches.en: ribbons on vegetables at a village show
branches.cn: 村里评比中系在蔬菜上的绶带

branches.en: the same judgement, given once as an object and once as a label
branches.cn: 同一种评判，一次给成物件，一次给成标签

intro.en: The word goes back to one Latin noun of value, a Latin verb of valuing, and the French forms that split into two English words; the eight entries keep that fork visible.
intro.cn: 这个词上溯到一个表示价值的拉丁名词、一个表示估价的拉丁动词，以及分成两个英语词的法语词形；下面八条让这个分岔看得见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun pretium and the verb built on it are directly recorded, which is why price, prize and praise can all be traced to one source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 pretium 以及由它构成的动词都有直接记录，所以 price、prize、praise 才能一同追到同一个源头。

items.meaning: a reward given to a winner

definition_zh: 明智的；聪明的；有智慧的；（口语）知晓的；以…方式
definition_en: having or showing good judgement built from experience, and in spoken use, knowing about something
core_image: 一个人抬手示意同伴先别急，等对方把话说完才点头回了一句
scene: 朋友刚要发火，他抬手示意先别急，等对方把话讲完才慢慢点头。 It was a wise decision to leave before the storm began.
sceneCN: 这里 wise 是「明智的」（第 1 个义项：判断得当、有分寸）；句意为在风暴来临前离开是明智的决定。抬手示意别急的那一下，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 明智的；有智慧的；（口语）知晓的

senses.title: Judging well from experience
senses.definition: able to see what matters and choose the right way, especially because of long experience
senses.definitionCN: 能看清什么要紧并选对做法，尤其因长期经验而如此
senses.example: It was a wise decision to leave before the storm began.
senses.exampleCN: 在风暴来临前离开是明智的决定。
senses.why: The old adjective simply described someone who knows, and knowing how to act came to be the heart of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老形容词最初只形容某人知道，后来懂得如何行动成了它的核心。

senses.title: In spoken use: aware of
senses.definition: in informal speech, knowing about something, often something hidden or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中表示知道某事，常指隐藏或不愉快的事
senses.example: She was wise to their tricks and refused to sign.
senses.exampleCN: 她看穿了他们的把戏，拒绝签字。
senses.why: The informal sense keeps the old idea of knowing, but strips away the judgement and leaves mere awareness.
senses.whyCN: 口语义保留了古老「知道」的观念，却剥掉了判断，只剩知晓。

senses.title: As a suffix: in the way of
senses.definition: attached to a noun to mean with regard to that thing, as in money-wise or stepwise
senses.definitionCN: 接在名词后表示就某方面而言或按某种方式，如 money-wise、stepwise
senses.example: Clockwise means turning in the direction of a clock.
senses.exampleCN: clockwise 意为沿钟表指示的方向旋转。
senses.why: A separate suffix -wise came from the same root and means manner, which is why it attaches so freely.
senses.whyCN: 另有一个来自同一词根的后缀 -wise 表示方式，所以它能自由地黏在各种词上。

intro.en: Wise is a Germanic adjective of knowing, Old English wīs, related to the verb that gave wit, and to the noun wisdom.
intro.cn: wise 是日耳曼语中表示「知道」的形容词，古英语 wīs，与产生 wit 的动词同源，也与 wisdom 相关。

items.en: The root meant to see or to know, and the same family gave German wissen, to know.
items.cn: 这个词根意为看见或知道，同族给了德语 wissen（知道）。

items.en: wīs described a person of knowledge and sound counsel, used of rulers and elders.
items.cn: wīs 形容有知识、能给出好建议的人，用于统治者与长者。

items.en: The adjective kept its shape and paired with -dom to name the quality itself.
items.cn: 这个形容词形式未变，与 -dom 结合来命名品质本身。

items.en: The suffix -wise began to mean manner in compound adverbs such as clockwise.
items.cn: 词尾 -wise 开始在 clockwise 这类复合副词中表示方式。

items.en: Spoken English added the lighter sense of simply being aware, as in wise to a trick.
items.cn: 口头英语又添加了仅表示知晓的轻义，如 wise to a trick。

note.en: The first group holds near twins of spelling, the second other adjectives of good judgement.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近的词，第二组收其他表示判断良好的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun of the same family.
To go upwards.
A rare spelling variant of wise.
A clever joking remark.
Showing practical good sense.
Careful about the future, avoiding risk.
Showing a lack of sense.

normalIntro.en: Wise is a short word with a long history; link it to wit and wisdom rather than to spelling tricks.
normalIntro.cn: wise 词短史长；把它和 wit、wisdom 连起来，比靠拼写技巧更牢。

normal.en: Wise and wit share a root: both are about knowing.
normal.cn: wise 和 wit 同根：都与「知道」有关。

normal.en: Add dom to get wisdom, the state of being wise.
normal.cn: 加 dom 得到 wisdom，即明智的状态。

normal.en: The past of rise is rose, and rise looks close, but wise needs the z sound.
normal.cn: rise 的过去式是 rose，看起来相近，但 wise 发的是 z 音。

normal.en: Money-wise means where money is concerned: the suffix means with regard to.
normal.cn: money-wise 意为就钱而言：这个后缀表示「就…而言」。

normal.en: A wise choice usually looks boring at the time and obvious years later.
normal.cn: 明智的选择当时看着平淡，多年之后显得理所当然。

abstract.en: A hand raised to slow a friend down.
abstract.cn: 一只抬起的手，让朋友慢一点。

abstract.en: A nod after listening, not during.
abstract.cn: 听完之后的点头，而不是听到一半就点。

abstract.en: A step taken carefully, then a second one.
abstract.cn: 先迈出小心的第一步，再迈第二步。

examples.en: It would be wise to check the figures twice.
examples.cn: 把数字核对两遍是明智的。

examples.en: She gave me some wise advice about saving money.
examples.cn: 她给了我一些关于存钱的明智建议。

examples.en: He is wise to their plan and will not join it.
examples.cn: 他看穿了他们的计划，不会参与。

dict_mnemonic.text: wit（智力）+ -ise 的读音相近 —— 有智力又能用对，就是「明智的」。

root: 日耳曼语词根（看见、知道）→ 古英语 wīs（明智的）→ wise；同族有 wisdom、wisely、wit。

sensesIntro.en: From the deep judgement of the old, the word lightens in speech to mere awareness, and lives on as a suffix meaning in the manner of.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从长者的深厚判断，在口语里变轻为单纯知晓，并作为表示方式的后缀继续存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand that asks for a moment of thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抬起、要求稍作思考的手。

branches.en: The judgement branch: leaving before the storm.
The awareness branch: wise to a trick.
branches.cn: 知晓分支：看穿一个把戏。

branches.en: The suffix branch: clockwise, money-wise.
The lightness branch: knowing without judging.
branches.cn: 轻义分支：知道而不评判。

branches.en: The practical branch: sense turned into a way of doing things.
branches.cn: 务实分支：判断力化为做事的方式。

intro.en: Wise stands alone and also works as a suffix meaning manner; with -dom and -ly it builds the rest of its family.
intro.cn: wise 可以单独使用，也能当表示方式的后缀；配上 -dom 与 -ly 便构成它的其余家族。

latinIntro.en: The adjective is Germanic; the Latin entries give borrowed words for the same virtue.
latinIntro.cn: 这个形容词属于日耳曼语；拉丁条目给出表达同一美德的借入词。

items.example: The adjective turned into an action.
The wit sense pressed into a joke.
items.exampleCN: 机智义被压进一个笑话。

items.example: The ending marks degrees of judgement.

definition_zh: 文章；冠词；物品
definition_en: a piece of writing in a paper, or a word like a or the, or a single object
core_image: 摊开的报纸上一篇带标题的文章
scene: 早晨，一个人摊开报纸，读一篇关于新公园的文章。 She read an article about the new park.
sceneCN: 这里 article 是「文章」（第 1 个义项：报刊上的一篇文字）；句意为她读了一篇关于新公园的文章。

senses.title: A piece of writing
senses.definition: a piece of writing on a subject in a newspaper or a magazine
senses.definitionCN: 报刊或杂志上关于某个主题的一篇文字
senses.example: She read an article about the new park.
senses.exampleCN: 她读了一篇关于新公园的文章。
senses.why: A small part cut from a larger text is the first sense of the Latin word.
senses.whyCN: 从大文本中分出来的一个小块，就是这个词的拉丁第一义。

senses.title: A grammatical word
senses.definition: a small word such as a, an or the used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前的小词，如 a、an 或 the
senses.example: The word the is a definite article.
senses.exampleCN: the 这个词是定冠词。
senses.why: Grammar also cuts small separate words out of a sentence, and these keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 语法同样从句子中分出独立的小词，这些词沿用同一名称。

senses.title: A single object
senses.definition: one object of a particular kind
senses.definitionCN: 某一类的单件物品
senses.example: The shop sells small articles for the home.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售家用小件物品。
senses.why: An item in a set is another separate piece, which gives the sense of a single object.
senses.whyCN: 一套中的一件也是独立的一块，于是有「单件物品」的义项。

intro.en: The recorded history of article is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 article 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Articulus meant a small joint or a small part.
items.cn: articulus 意为小关节或小部分。

items.en: Ars meant skill, and it stands behind articulus.
items.cn: ars 意为技艺，是 articulus 的来源之一。

items.en: French article named a separate part of a text.
items.cn: 法语 article 指文本中独立的一部分。

items.en: English used article for a section of writing.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪用 article 指文字中的一节。

items.en: Today it also covers grammar words and single goods.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖语法小词与单件商品。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one piece of writing or object.
entries.definitionCN: 指多篇文章或多件物品。

entries.definition: It looks close but means a tiny piece of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 外观相近，但指极小的物质微粒。

entries.definition: The verb for speaking clearly in parts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指清晰地分节表达。

entries.definition: A general word for one part of something.
It stresses news told in an organised way.
entries.definitionCN: 强调有条理地讲述新闻。

entries.definition: It names one thing in a list or a set.
entries.definitionCN: 指清单或一套中的一件。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Articulus meant a small part: an article is one piece marked off inside a bigger text or set.
normal.cn: articulus 意为小部分：article 就是大文本或大集合中被分出来的一块。

normal.en: The same family also gives articles and articulate.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 articles 与 articulate。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase read an article.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「读一篇文章」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of article in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 article 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: a piece of writing in a paper, or a word like a or the, or a single object.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「文章」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a headed article spread open in a newspaper.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的报纸上一篇带标题的文章。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She read an article about the new park.
examples.cn: 她读了一篇关于新公园的文章。

examples.en: The word the is a definite article.
examples.cn: the 这个词是定冠词。

examples.en: The shop sells small articles for the home.
examples.cn: 这家店出售家用小件物品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提克尔」——报纸上一篇带标题的文章：文章

root: article 来自拉丁语 articulus「小关节、小部分」，与 ars「技艺」相关，经法语 article 进入英语；十三世纪指文字中的一节，今天也涵盖语法小词与单件商品。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of article grows from one core image: a headed article spread open in a newspaper.
sensesIntro.cn: article 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：摊开的报纸上一篇带标题的文章。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a headed article spread open in a newspaper
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的报纸上一篇带标题的文章

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: A piece of writing.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：文章。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: A grammatical word.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：冠词。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: A piece of writing / A grammatical word.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：文章、冠词。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: A single object.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：物品。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the outer edge of the meaning: A piece of writing / A single object.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖意义的边缘：文章、物品。

intro.en: article can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: article 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It comes from articulus, a small joint.
items.exampleCN: 它来自 articulus，意为小关节。

items.example: It marks a small thing, as in article.
It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 放松；放宽；缓和
definition_en: to become less tense in body or mind; to make a rule or a limit less strict; to become less tight or less severe
core_image: 一直攥紧的拳头在长椅上慢慢松开
scene: 他在长椅上坐了很久，一直攥紧的拳头才慢慢松开。 A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
sceneCN: 这里 relax 是「放松」（第 1 个义项：身体或心情由紧张转为松弛）；句意为长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。画面里可留意：慢慢松开的拳头、长椅。

senses.title: To become less tense
senses.definition: to let the body or the mind become loose and calm
senses.definitionCN: 让身体或心情变得松弛平静
senses.example: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and the prefix adds a returning: tension that has tightened is let back to its resting state.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使松」，前缀则添上「回」的意味：绷紧的张力被放回到休息状态。

senses.title: To make a rule less strict
senses.definition: to make a rule, a limit, or a control less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、限制或管制不那么严格
senses.example: The city relaxed the rules on street markets last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天放宽了街头集市的规定。
senses.why: A rule can be tight like a muscle, and loosening it is described with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 规则可以像肌肉一样紧绷，而松开它用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To become less tight
senses.definition: to become less firm, less intense, or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么紧、不那么强烈或不那么严重
senses.example: His grip on the rail relaxed once the ship was steady.
senses.exampleCN: 船稳下来之后，他抓着栏杆的手松了。
senses.why: Here the loosening is physical again, but the object is a hold or a tension rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的松弛又回到物理层面，只是对象是握力或张力，而不是一个人。

intro.en: Relax is to loosen: the Latin adjective for loose becomes a verb, and the prefix sets the loosening in motion.
intro.cn: relax 意为「使松」：拉丁语表「松」的形容词变成动词，前缀让这一松开得以进行。

items.en: Laxus meant loose, slack, or wide, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: laxus 意为松的、松弛的或宽的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen, slacken, or let go.
items.cn: laxare 意为放松、使松弛或放开。

items.en: Relaxare added re- and meant to loosen back, to unbend, or to relieve.
items.cn: relaxare 加上 re-，意为松回去、舒展或缓解。

items.en: French relaxer carried the medical sense of easing tension into English.
items.cn: 法语 relaxer 把「缓解紧张」这一医学用法带入英语。

items.en: English widened the verb from muscles and minds to rules, prices, and controls.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词从肌肉与心情扩展到规则、价格与管制。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for loose; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resting and easing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语表「松」的形容词构成的词；近义组收表示休息与缓解的动词。

entries.definition: Not strict or not tight.
The act of relaxing.
Calm and not tense.
To stop activity and recover.
To make less tight.
To make less severe or painful.
To relax after work or stress.

normalIntro.en: The word is loosen plus back: a muscle, a rule, or a grip is allowed to return to slack.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「松开加回来」：肌肉、规则或握力被允许回到松弛。

normal.en: Laxus means loose, and relax means to make loose again.
normal.cn: laxus 意为松，relax 意为重新放松。

normal.en: Relax the rules means let them be less strict.
normal.cn: relax the rules 指让规定不那么严。

normal.en: A relaxed person is one whose shoulders have come down.
normal.cn: a relaxed person 就是肩膀放下来的人。

normal.en: The adjective relaxing describes what does the loosening.
normal.cn: 形容词 relaxing 描述起松弛作用的东西。

normal.en: Release and relax are different words; one lets go, one slackens.
normal.cn: release 与 relax 是两个词：一个放开，一个松弛。

abstract.en: To relax is to stop holding what no longer needs holding.
abstract.cn: 放松，就是停止握住已经不必握住的东西。

abstract.en: A mind that never slackens cannot tell what matters.
abstract.cn: 从不松弛的心，分不清什么要紧。

abstract.en: Some rules deserve to be loosened, and some only appear to.
abstract.cn: 有些规则值得放宽，有些只是看起来如此。

examples.en: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
examples.cn: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。

examples.en: The city relaxed the rules on street markets last spring.
examples.cn: 这座城市去年春天放宽了街头集市的规定。

examples.en: His grip on the rail relaxed once the ship was steady.
examples.cn: 船稳下来之后，他抓着栏杆的手松了。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 lax（松）：把紧绷的肌肉放回松弛，是放松；把绷紧的规定放回松弛，是放宽。

root: 拉丁 laxus（松的）→ laxare（使松）→ relaxare（松回去、缓解）→ 法语 relaxer → 英语 relax；同族有 relaxation、relaxed、relaxing，形近的 lax 也出自 laxus。

sensesIntro.en: The core is slackening; the senses move from a tense body, to a strict rule, to a tight hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「变松」；义项从紧绷的身体，到严格的规定，再到握紧的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist that has been clenched for hours slowly opening on a bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：一直攥紧的拳头在长椅上慢慢松开。

branches.en: a bath after a long shift
a market rule made easier
a hand letting go of a rail
a body and a grip both loosening
a rule and a mind both eased
branches.cn: 被放宽的规定与松弛下来的心

intro.en: The Latin adjective for loose becomes a verb of loosening, and the prefix turns the action into a return to slack.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「松」的形容词变成表「使松」的动词，前缀把这一动作变成「松回去」。

latinIntro.en: The base is laxus, loose; laxare means to loosen, and re- means back.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 laxus（松的）；laxare 意为使松，re- 表「往回」。

definition_zh: 侧面；一边；方面；一方
definition_en: a surface at the left or right, an aspect, or one group in a dispute
core_image: 一个立方体翻过来，露出旁边另外一面
scene: 他指着房间的一侧，请人把箱子搬过去。 Please move the box to this side.
sceneCN: 这里 side 是「一边」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把箱子搬到这一边。

senses.title: A surface at the left or right
senses.definition: one of the surfaces or positions to the left or right
senses.definitionCN: 左面或右面的一侧
senses.example: Please move the box to this side.
senses.exampleCN: 请把箱子搬到这一边。
senses.why: This is the basic spatial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的空间义项。

senses.title: An aspect
senses.definition: one part of a situation or problem
senses.definitionCN: 情况或问题的一个方面
senses.example: We must look at every side of the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须看问题的每个方面。
senses.why: A thing has sides in space and in thought.
senses.whyCN: 事物在空间中有侧面，在思考中也有方面。

senses.title: One group in a dispute
senses.definition: one of the groups taking part in an argument or game
senses.definitionCN: 争论或比赛中参与的一方
senses.example: Both sides agreed to talk.
senses.exampleCN: 双方同意交谈。
senses.why: People line up on opposite sides like two edges.
senses.whyCN: 人分站两边，就像两条边。

intro.en: Side once meant the flank of the body.
intro.cn: side 最初指身体的侧面。

items.en: Side meant a flank or a long edge.
items.cn: side 意为肋部或长边。

items.en: The related word sitha also meant side.
items.cn: 相关词 sitha 同样表示侧面。

items.en: The word spread to land, rooms, and roads.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到土地、房间和道路。

items.en: The sense of aspect appeared.
items.cn: 「方面」的义项出现了。

items.en: The sense of a team or party appeared.
items.cn: 「一方、队伍」的义项出现了。

note.en: Side is compared with similar-looking words and with words for edges.
note.cn: 把 side 与形近词以及表示边缘的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where something is or happens
to breathe out slowly
a mark with a meaning
the outer line of something
the side of the body
one part of a situation

normalIntro.en: Side is always the part beside you.
normalIntro.cn: side 永远是身旁的那一面。

normal.en: Please move the box to this side.
normal.cn: 请把箱子搬到这一边。

normal.en: They sat side by side.
normal.cn: 他们并排坐着。

normal.en: Both sides agreed to talk.
normal.cn: 双方同意交谈。

normal.en: The shop is on the other side.
normal.cn: 商店在另一边。

normal.en: He took my side in the argument.
normal.cn: 争论中他站在我这边。

abstract.en: Every coin has two sides.
abstract.cn: 每枚硬币都有两面。

abstract.en: A side is a door into a whole.
abstract.cn: 一个侧面是通向整体的门。

abstract.en: To choose a side is to choose a story.
abstract.cn: 选边站就是选择一个故事。

examples.en: Please move the box to this side.
examples.cn: 请把箱子搬到这一边。

examples.en: We must look at every side of the problem.
examples.cn: 我们必须看问题的每个方面。

examples.en: Both sides agreed to talk.
examples.cn: 双方同意交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: side 的核心是旁边那一面：路的两旁是 side，争论的两边也是 side。

root: 源自古英语 side（肋部、侧面），核心义「旁边的一面」。

sensesIntro.en: Side means a surface at the left or right, an aspect, or one party.
sensesIntro.cn: side 意为侧面、方面或一方。

core.en: The face beside the main face.
core.cn: 主面旁边的那个面。

branches.en: A box has six sides.
A problem has many sides.
Two sides meet to talk.
Space and thought both have sides.
The physical edge becomes a team.

intro.en: Side builds words for edges, paths, and directions.
intro.cn: side 构成表示边缘、路径和方向的词。

latinIntro.en: Side is Germanic; Latin latus, side, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: side 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 latus（侧面）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The side of the house is white.

items.meaning: an extra result of a medicine
items.example: The drug has few side effects.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几乎没有副作用。

items.meaning: a smaller street off a main road
items.example: They parked on a side street.

items.meaning: showing only one point of view

items.example: The two houses stand side by side.

definition_zh: 线；排；行；线条；台词；线路；排队
definition_en: a long narrow mark; a row of people or things; written words in a row; words spoken by an actor; a wire carrying messages; to stand in a row
core_image: 一根拉直的细绳，从这头到那头
scene: 开学第一课，他用粉笔在黑板上划下一条直线。 Please line up outside the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 line 是动词「排队」（第 7 个义项：站成一排）；句意为请在大厅外排好队。

derivatives.zh: line 加拉丁式后缀 -ar，指「线的；线性的」
out 与 line 合成，指「轮廓；大纲」

senses.title: A long narrow mark
senses.definition: a long thin mark on a surface or an imagined one
senses.definitionCN: 表面细长的痕迹或想象中的线
senses.example: Draw a straight line between the two points.
senses.exampleCN: 在两点之间画一条直线。
senses.why: Stretched thread is the plain picture: one direction, no width.
senses.whyCN: 拉直的细绳是最朴素的画面：只有方向，没有宽度。

senses.title: A row of people or things
senses.definition: people or things standing one behind or beside another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物前后或左右排成一行
senses.example: A long line formed outside the bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 面包房外排起了长队。
senses.why: Things arranged along the thread become a row.
senses.whyCN: 沿细绳排开的物就成了一行。

senses.title: Written words in a row
senses.definition: a row of written or printed words
senses.definitionCN: 一行书写或印刷的文字
senses.example: Read the first line of each paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 读每段的第一行。
senses.why: Writing follows the same stretched thread across the page.
senses.whyCN: 书写沿着同一条「细绳」横过纸面。

senses.title: Words an actor speaks
senses.definition: words an actor memorizes and says
senses.definitionCN: 演员背熟并说出的词句
senses.example: He forgot his lines in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 他在第二幕忘了台词。
senses.why: Each spoken sentence is one row of the script.
senses.whyCN: 每句台词都是剧本中的一行。

senses.title: A wire or route carrying messages or transport
senses.definition: a wire carrying calls, or a route of buses, ships or trains
senses.definitionCN: 传电话的电线，或公交、船、火车的线路
senses.example: The phone line is busy.
senses.exampleCN: 电话占线。
senses.why: A route drawn across a map is a thread of travel or signal.
senses.whyCN: 地图上画出的路线就是行程或信号的「细绳」。

senses.title: A boundary or limit
senses.definition: a limit that should not be crossed
senses.definitionCN: 不应越过的一条界限
senses.example: Crossing that line costs trust.
senses.exampleCN: 越过那条线会失去信任。
senses.why: A thread drawn on the ground says: beyond this, stop.
senses.whyCN: 在地上拉一根绳，意思就是：过此即止。

senses.title: To stand or arrange in a row
senses.definition: to form or put into a row
senses.definitionCN: 排成一行或使成行
senses.example: Please line up outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 请在大厅外排好队。
senses.why: The noun hardened into a verb: making rows.
senses.whyCN: 名词固化为动词：制造行列。

senses.title: To cover the inside of
senses.definition: to put a layer of material on the inside of something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物内侧加一层材料
senses.example: Line the tin with baking paper.
senses.exampleCN: 在烤模里垫上烘焙纸。
senses.why: An inner layer "lines" the walls from within.
senses.whyCN: 内层从内部「沿线」贴附于壁。

intro.en: Line comes from Old French ligne, from Latin linea 'linen thread', from linum 'flax'; the stretched thread of flax gave every kind of line its name.
intro.cn: line 来自古法语 ligne，出自拉丁语 linea「亚麻线」（linum「亚麻」）；亚麻拉成的细线给各种「线」命了名。

items.en: Latin linum meant flax, the plant whose fibres made thread.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linum 指亚麻，其纤维可制线。

items.en: Latin linea meant a linen thread, then a drawn line, then a row.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linea 先指亚麻线，继指画线，再指行列。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the senses of thread, stroke and row.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 承载线、笔画与行列诸义。

items.en: In Middle English line spread to writing rows, acting scripts and routes.
items.cn: 中古英语把 line 扩展到书写行、台词与路线。

items.en: Modern English added telephone lines, industry boundaries and the verb of lining garments.
items.cn: 现代英语新增电话线路、行业界线与给衣物衬里的动词。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists thread and row words.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出线与行列之词。

entries.definition: Made of or along lines.
An arm or leg; shares three letters, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 臂或腿；共享三字母，词根无关。

entries.definition: The inner covering layer of a garment.
Things side by side; line can also mean front-to-back.
entries.definitionCN: 并排之物；line 也可指前后纵列。

entries.definition: People waiting one behind another, chiefly British.
entries.definitionCN: 排队等候的人群，多用于英式。

entries.definition: The physical original of the word.
The edge of an area; matches the limit sense.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the flax trail and real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用亚麻词路与真实短语。

normal.en: Latin linea meant linen thread, from linum, flax.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 linea 指亚麻线，出自 linum（亚麻）。

normal.en: Cousins: linear, lining, outline.
normal.cn: 同族词：linear、lining、outline。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: line up, in line with, hold the line, the bottom line.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：排队、与……一致、别挂断、底线。

normal.en: Actors forget lines; callers hold the line.
normal.cn: 演员忘台词；打电话的人别挂线。

normal.en: Draw a line between work and rest means set a limit.
normal.cn: 在work与rest之间draw a line 意为划定界限。

abstract.en: Picture one flax thread pulled tight between two nails.
abstract.cn: 想象一根亚麻线在两枚钉子间绷直。

abstract.en: Picture chalk crossing a blackboard in one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象粉笔一笔横过黑板。

abstract.en: Picture coats turned inside out, smooth linings showing.
abstract.cn: 想象大衣翻过来，露出平整的衬里。

examples.en: Sign your name on the dotted line.
examples.cn: 在虚线上签下你的名字。

examples.en: People lined the streets to watch the parade.
examples.cn: 人们沿街排开观看游行。

examples.en: Her speech stayed in line with party policy.
examples.cn: 她的发言与党的政策保持一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来恩」——一根线连来恩情 → 线；排队

root: 拉丁语 linum「亚麻」→ linea「亚麻线」→ 古法语 ligne → 英语 line；由拉直的细线引申出行、台词、线路与界限。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all follow one stretched thread: drawn marks, standing rows, written rows, spoken rows, routes, limits, making rows, and inner layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都循着同一根绷紧的线：画痕、人列、书写行、台词行、路线、界限、排队的动作与内层衬里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread pulled tight from one point to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一点绷到另一点的线。

branches.en: THE DRAWN MARK: the thread turned into geometry.
branches.cn: 画出的线：细绳变成了几何。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS ROWS: standing in line and lining others up.
branches.cn: 人成行列：自己排队与让他人列队。

branches.en: WORDS IN ROWS: printed lines and actor lines.
branches.cn: 成行的文字：印刷行与演员台词。

branches.en: THE LONG CONNECTION: routes, wires and boundaries.
branches.cn: 长长的连接：路线、电线与界线。

branches.en: THE INNER THREAD: lining clings close to the walls.
branches.cn: 内在的线：衬里紧贴内壁。

intro.en: Line is a borrowed noun with no prefixes; the family grows with Latin-style and native suffixes.
intro.cn: line 是无前缀的外来名词；词族靠拉丁式与本族后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root linea gives true cousins like linear and lineage; the items also show English suffix work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 linea 提供 linear、lineage 等真表亲；条目亦展示英语后缀加工。

items.example: Cars lined up at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 汽车在大门口排起长队。

items.example: A cousin of the same root.

definition_zh: 战争；战事；斗争
definition_en: fighting between countries or groups with weapons over a long period
core_image: 地图上的两条战线，中间夹着一段没有人敢耕的地
scene: 旧相册里有一张黑白照片，几个年轻人站在泥里，背景是烧了一半的村子。 The country was at war for more than ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 war 是「战争」（第 1 个义项：国家或群体之间长期持械交战）；句意为这个国家打了十多年仗。地图上两条战线的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Fighting between nations
senses.definition: organized armed fighting between countries or large groups, lasting over time
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大团体之间长期组织的持械交战
senses.example: The country was at war for more than ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家打了十多年仗。
senses.why: The word grew next to a Germanic form of the same base that also gave worse, and the meaning settled on armed conflict.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与同基底表示「更糟」的日耳曼语形式并行生长，词义最后落定在持械冲突上。

senses.title: A campaign against something
senses.definition: a determined effort to defeat a problem, such as disease or poverty
senses.definitionCN: 为克服疾病、贫困等问题而作的坚决努力
senses.example: The city began a war on rats in the old sewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市开始了一场治理旧下水道鼠患的战争。
senses.why: Modern English extends the word to any long struggle that needs organized effort.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把这个词扩展到任何需要组织起来的长期斗争。

senses.title: A struggle between ideas
senses.definition: in phrases such as a war of words, a fierce exchange of hostile speech
senses.definitionCN: 在 a war of words 等短语中指激烈的相互指责
senses.example: The debate turned into a war of words between the two professors.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论变成了两位教授之间的一场论战。
senses.why: Words that are exchanged like blows are described as a war, though nothing is broken.
senses.whyCN: 像拳脚一样来回抛的言语被叫作战争，尽管什么也没被打破。

senses.title: The state of being at war
senses.definition: the condition of opposing forces, as in war and peace
senses.definitionCN: 敌对力量相持的状态，如 war and peace 并用
senses.example: The novel opens in the year before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从战争前一年写起。
senses.why: English names the condition as well as the events, so one can live in the year before it.
senses.whyCN: 英语既命名事件也命名状态，所以人可以在它开始前的那一年里生活。

intro.en: War comes from Old Northern French werre, which spread from a Germanic word for confusion or disorder.
intro.cn: war 来自古北法语 werre，而后者源自日耳曼语表示混乱、纷扰的词。

items.en: A Germanic word for confusion or strife lies behind the French form, related to a form that gave worse.
items.cn: 法语词形背后是一个表示混乱、纷争的日耳曼语词，与给出 worse 的词形相关。

items.en: Old Northern French werre meant war, and Norman French brought it to England.
items.cn: 古北法语 werre 意为战争，诺曼法语把它带到英格兰。

items.en: English had its own word, werre, and the two forms settled into war.
items.cn: 英语本有 werre 一词，两种形式最后定形为 war。

items.en: The word was used of sieges and campaigns, and only later of wars between states.
items.cn: 这个词曾用于围城与战役，后来才专指国家之间的战争。

items.en: Modern English adds the war on disease and the war of words, both borrowed from bodily fighting.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出抗击疾病的战争与论战，都借自真实的打斗。

note.en: The first group gathers the fighting family, the second the words for conflicts of different scale.
note.cn: 第一组收战争词族，第二组收不同规模的冲突词。

entries.definition: The plural form, short and easily confused with wears.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，易与 wears 相混

entries.definition: The activity of fighting, of any kind.
A fighter, often in older writing.
In conflict with each other.
One armed fight, smaller than a war.
A broad word for any clash.
A planned series of actions in a war.
The state of not fighting.

normalIntro.en: War is a short old word with a long shadow; keep it apart from its look-alike wear.
normalIntro.cn: war 是个短小的古词，影子却长；记它时要与形近的 wear 分开。

normal.en: War is short and hard, like the thing itself.
normal.cn: war 又短又硬，正如它所表示的。

normal.en: Wear, with an e, means to have on or to erode.
normal.cn: wear 带 e，指穿或磨损。

normal.en: Be at war is the state; declare war is the act.
normal.cn: be at war 是状态，declare war 是行为。

normal.en: Warfare is the activity; warrior is the person.
normal.cn: warfare 是活动，warrior 是人。

normal.en: A war of words is loud and bloodless.
normal.cn: a war of words 是吵闹却不见血的。

abstract.en: See two lines on a map with empty ground between.
abstract.cn: 想地图上两条线，中间是一片空着的地。

abstract.en: Smell burnt timber in a half-ruined village.
abstract.cn: 闻半毁村落里焦木的气味。

abstract.en: Hear two professors raising their voices, not their hands.
abstract.cn: 听两位教授提高的是嗓门而不是手。

examples.en: The war lasted four years and changed the country.
examples.cn: 这场战争持续四年，改变了这个国家。

examples.en: Doctors are waging a war on smoking.
examples.cn: 医生们正在开展一场控烟的战争。

examples.en: After the war the town was slowly rebuilt.
examples.cn: 战后这座小镇被慢慢重建起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇」——警报一响，人人「哇」的一声跑开，那就是它。

root: 日耳曼语「混乱、纷争」→ 古北法语 werre（战争）→ 中古英语 war。

sensesIntro.en: Armed fighting gives the core, and the word then lends itself to campaigns against disease, to verbal battles and to the plain state of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 持械交战是核心，这个词随后又借给抗病之战、言语论战以及抽象的冲突状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines with empty ground between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条战线夹着空出的地。

branches.en: The nations branch: ten years of fighting.
The campaign branch: doctors against smoking.
branches.cn: 活动分支：医生对付吸烟。

branches.en: The words branch: two professors out loud.
branches.cn: 言语分支：两位教授的对吵。

branches.en: The state branch: the year before it began.
branches.cn: 状态分支：开始前的那一年。

branches.en: The peace branch: war and peace set against each other.
branches.cn: 和平分支：战争与和平相对并列。

intro.en: War is a whole word; its family comes from English compounds and endings such as -fare, -ior and -like.
intro.cn: war 是整词，词族由 -fare、-ior、-like 等英语后缀与复合构成。

latinIntro.en: The word came through French from a Germanic root, with no Latin source, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼词根经法语传入，没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The form that came to England.
It forms warhead, the front of a missile.
